lines.text: **BINDING TERM SHEET**
**Acquisition of 100% of the Outstanding Equity Interests of** **Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc.**
Dated as of September 10, 2025

This Binding Term Sheet (this \"Term Sheet\") sets forth the principal terms and conditions agreed upon by the parties identified below with respect to the proposed acquisition described herein. Except as set forth in Section 18 (Binding Provisions) below, this Term Sheet is intended to be binding on the parties and shall govern the preparation of the Definitive Agreement (as defined below). This Term Sheet supersedes and replaces in its entirety the non-binding Letter of Intent dated August 15, 2025 (the \"LOI\"), previously entered into between Whitmore Capital Partners LLC and Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc. with respect to the proposed acquisition of Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc. Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the context in which they appear.
**[Section 1: Parties]{.underline}**

**Buyer:** Whitmore Capital Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, with its principal offices at 200 South Wacker Drive, Suite 3100, Chicago, Illinois 60606 (referred to herein as \"Buyer\" or \"Whitmore\").

**Seller:** Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc., a Delaware corporation, with its principal offices at 1550 NW Everett Street, Suite 800, Portland, Oregon 97209 (referred to herein as \"Seller\" or \"Evergreen\").

**Target / the Company:** Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc., an Oregon corporation, with its principal offices at 8700 SW Tualatin-Sherwood Road, Suite 200, Tualatin, Oregon 97062 (referred to herein as \"Target,\" \"Cascadia,\" or the \"Company\").

Seller is the sole stockholder of Target, holding one hundred percent (100%) of the issued and outstanding shares of common stock of Target, consisting of 1,000,000 shares of common stock, par value \$0.01 per share (the \"Shares\"). No other shares of capital stock or other equity interests of the Company are issued or outstanding as of the date of this Term Sheet.
**[Section 2: Transaction Structure]{.underline}**

**Stock Purchase.** Buyer shall acquire from Seller, and Seller shall sell, assign, transfer, and deliver to Buyer, all 1,000,000 issued and outstanding Shares, representing one hundred percent (100%) of the issued and outstanding equity interests of the Company. As of the date of this Term Sheet, no options, warrants, convertible securities, or other instruments convertible into or exercisable or exchangeable for equity interests of the Company are outstanding, and Seller shall represent and warrant to such effect in the Definitive Agreement. Following the Closing (as defined below), the Company will be a wholly-owned subsidiary of Buyer.

**Definitive Agreement.** The transaction shall be documented in a definitive Stock Purchase Agreement (the \"Definitive Agreement\" or the \"SPA\"), which shall be prepared in the first instance by Seller\'s counsel, Fortuna & Blake LLP, and delivered to Buyer\'s counsel, Ashford, Pennington & Yates LLP, for review and negotiation. The Definitive Agreement shall contain the terms and conditions set forth in this Term Sheet, together with such additional terms and conditions as are customary for transactions of this nature and as may be mutually agreed by the parties. The Definitive Agreement shall be consistent with the terms of this Term Sheet in all material respects. In the event of a conflict between this Term Sheet and the Definitive Agreement, the parties shall negotiate in good faith to resolve such conflict; provided, however, that the economic terms set forth herein (including without limitation the Base Enterprise Value, the purchase price formula, the indemnification cap and basket, the Special Indemnity terms, the escrow terms, and the earnout terms) shall control until expressly superseded by a mutually executed Definitive Agreement.
**[Section 3: Purchase Price]{.underline}**
**Base Enterprise Value.** The base enterprise value of the Company for purposes of this transaction shall be Two Hundred Fifteen Million Dollars (\$215,000,000) (the \"Base Enterprise Value\").
**Purchase Price Formula.** The purchase price to be paid by Buyer to Seller for the Shares (the \"Purchase Price\") shall be calculated as follows:
> Purchase Price = Base Enterprise Value + Estimated Closing Net Working Capital -- Estimated Closing Indebtedness -- Estimated Seller Transaction Expenses

**Target Net Working Capital.** The target net working capital for the Company (the \"Target NWC\") shall be Eighteen Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$18,200,000), calculated in accordance with the methodology to be set forth in the Definitive Agreement and consistent with United States generally accepted accounting principles (\"GAAP\") as historically applied by the Company.

**Estimated Closing Statement.** Seller shall deliver to Buyer a good faith estimated closing statement (the \"Estimated Closing Statement\") setting forth Seller\'s reasonable estimates of (i) Closing Net Working Capital (\"Estimated Closing NWC\"), (ii) Closing Indebtedness (\"Estimated Closing Indebtedness\"), and (iii) Seller Transaction Expenses (\"Estimated Seller Transaction Expenses\"), in each case calculated as of the Closing Date, no later than three (3) business days prior to the Closing Date. The Estimated Closing Statement shall be prepared in accordance with GAAP as historically applied by the Company and in a manner consistent with the methodology to be set forth in the Definitive Agreement.
**Illustrative Calculation.** The following calculation is provided for reference purposes only and shall not be deemed to establish the actual Purchase Price or any component thereof:
**Component**                                 **Amount**
Base Enterprise Value                         \$215,000,000
Plus: Estimated Closing NWC                   \$18,200,000
Less: Estimated Closing Indebtedness          (\$42,300,000)
Less: Estimated Seller Transaction Expenses   (\$3,900,000)
**Estimated Closing Payment**                 **\$187,000,000**
For reference, the components of Estimated Closing Indebtedness and Estimated Seller Transaction Expenses used in the illustrative calculation above are as follows:
> *Estimated Closing Indebtedness (\$42,300,000):*
> • Senior term loan with Cascade Mutual Bank: \$28,000,000
> • Equipment financing with Pacific Lease Corp.: \$9,800,000
> • Subordinated seller note payable to Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc.: \$4,500,000
> *Estimated Seller Transaction Expenses (\$3,900,000):*
> • Seller\'s legal fees (Fortuna & Blake LLP): \$1,800,000
> • Seller\'s advisory fees: \$1,200,000
> • Other transaction costs (including accounting, transfer taxes, and miscellaneous): \$900,000

**Net Working Capital Adjustment.** The net working capital adjustment shall be calculated on a dollar-for-dollar basis from the first dollar (i.e., there shall be no collar or threshold). Following the Closing, Buyer shall prepare a final closing statement reflecting the actual Closing NWC, Closing Indebtedness, and Seller Transaction Expenses as of the Closing Date. The post-closing true-up process shall be completed within ninety (90) days following the Closing Date. Standard dispute resolution procedures, including referral to an independent accounting firm mutually acceptable to the parties for resolution of any disputed items, shall be set forth in the Definitive Agreement.
**[Section 4: Escrow]{.underline}**

**Escrow Amount.** At the Closing, Buyer shall deposit Sixteen Million One Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$16,125,000) (the \"Escrow Amount\"), which is equal to seven and one-half percent (7.5%) of the Base Enterprise Value (\$215,000,000 × 0.075 = \$16,125,000), with Pinnacle Trust Company, as escrow agent (the \"Escrow Agent\"), pursuant to an escrow agreement in customary form and substance to be agreed upon by the parties and the Escrow Agent (the \"Escrow Agreement\"). The Escrow Amount shall be deducted from the Purchase Price payable to Seller at Closing.

**Escrow Purpose.** The Escrow Amount shall serve as security for Seller\'s indemnification obligations under the Definitive Agreement. The Escrow Amount shall be the sole and exclusive source of recovery for Buyer\'s indemnification claims with respect to breaches of non-Fundamental Representations, up to the Escrow Amount; provided that claims for Losses exceeding the Escrow Amount (but subject to the Cap set forth in Section 8 below) may be pursued directly against Seller. For the avoidance of doubt, the escrow shall also serve as a source of recovery for claims under the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity as set forth in Section 9 below.
**Escrow Release Schedule.** The Escrow Amount shall be released in accordance with the following schedule:

> \(a\) *General Indemnification Claims (Non-Fundamental Representations):* The portion of the Escrow Amount allocable to general indemnification claims shall be released to Seller on the date that is eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date, less any amounts subject to pending and unresolved indemnification claims as of such date.

> \(b\) *Fundamental Representations and Special Indemnities:* The portion of the Escrow Amount allocable to Fundamental Representations and the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall be released to Seller on the date that is thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date, less any amounts subject to pending and unresolved indemnification claims as of such date.

Any portion of the Escrow Amount that is not subject to pending or unresolved indemnification claims as of the applicable release date shall be promptly released to Seller. The specific allocation of the Escrow Amount between general indemnification claims and Fundamental Representations/Special Indemnity claims shall be set forth in the Escrow Agreement.
**[Section 5: Earnout]{.underline}**

**Maximum Earnout Payment.** In addition to the Purchase Price, Buyer shall pay to Seller an earnout payment (the \"Earnout Payment\") of up to Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000), subject to the terms and conditions set forth below.

**Measurement Period.** The Earnout Payment shall be calculated based on the Company\'s financial performance during the trailing twelve-month (TTM) period ending December 31, 2026 (the \"Measurement Period\").

**Metric.** The Earnout Payment shall be based on the Company\'s Adjusted EBITDA for the Measurement Period. \"Adjusted EBITDA\" shall be calculated in a manner consistent with the Company\'s historical practice and as defined in the Definitive Agreement, and shall exclude the impact of purchase price accounting adjustments, transaction-related costs, integration costs, and any other items mutually agreed to be excluded by the parties as set forth in the Definitive Agreement.
**Threshold and Floor.**

> \(a\) *Full Earnout:* If the Company achieves TTM Adjusted EBITDA of Thirty-Eight Million Dollars (\$38,000,000) or more for the Measurement Period, the full Earnout Payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) shall be payable to Seller.
> \(b\) *Floor:* No Earnout Payment shall be payable if TTM Adjusted EBITDA for the Measurement Period is less than Thirty-Two Million Dollars (\$32,000,000).

> \(c\) *Pro-Rata Calculation:* If TTM Adjusted EBITDA for the Measurement Period is equal to or greater than Thirty-Two Million Dollars (\$32,000,000) but less than Thirty-Eight Million Dollars (\$38,000,000), the Earnout Payment shall be calculated on a linear interpolation basis in accordance with the following formula:
> which equals approximately \$4,166,667 per \$1,000,000 of Adjusted EBITDA above \$32,000,000.

**Earnout Covenant.** Buyer shall not take any action with the primary purpose of avoiding or reducing the Earnout Payment. For the avoidance of doubt, Buyer shall have no affirmative obligation to operate the Company\'s business in any particular manner, and nothing herein shall restrict Buyer\'s ability to operate, integrate, or restructure the Company\'s business in Buyer\'s sole discretion, provided that Buyer does not take actions with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment. The Definitive Agreement shall not impose on Buyer any obligation to maintain the Company as a separate entity, to maintain any particular level of capital expenditure, to retain any particular employees, or to refrain from any particular operational decisions, so long as any such actions are taken in the ordinary course of Buyer\'s management of the Company and not with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment.

**Payment.** The Earnout Payment, if any, shall be payable to Seller within sixty (60) days following the end of the Measurement Period. Buyer shall deliver to Seller a written calculation of Adjusted EBITDA for the Measurement Period, together with reasonable supporting detail, within forty-five (45) days following the end of the Measurement Period.
**Dispute Resolution.** Customary earnout dispute resolution procedures, including review by an independent accounting firm, shall be set forth in the Definitive Agreement.
**[Section 6: Closing Indebtedness Payoff Mechanics]{.underline}**

**Payoff Letters Required.** Seller shall deliver to Buyer, or shall cause to be delivered to Buyer, executed payoff letters from each holder of Target Indebtedness (including, without limitation, Cascade Mutual Bank (in respect of the senior term loan), Pacific Lease Corp. (in respect of the equipment financing), and Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc. (in respect of the subordinated seller note)) no later than three (3) business days prior to the Closing Date. Each payoff letter shall set forth, at a minimum: (i) the aggregate amount required to repay in full the applicable indebtedness as of the Closing Date (including all principal, accrued and unpaid interest, prepayment premiums, breakage costs, and any other amounts required to fully satisfy and discharge such indebtedness), (ii) wire transfer instructions for payment of the applicable payoff amount, and (iii) a commitment by the applicable lender or holder to release all liens, security interests, mortgages, pledges, and other encumbrances securing such indebtedness upon receipt of the payoff amount, together with such UCC-3 termination statements, lien release documents, and other instruments as may be required to evidence such release.

**Simultaneous Payoff at Closing.** All Target Indebtedness shall be repaid simultaneously at Closing through the closing funds flow. No Target Indebtedness shall remain outstanding following the Closing. Buyer shall cause the payoff amounts to be paid directly to the applicable lenders or holders at Closing in accordance with the wire transfer instructions set forth in the payoff letters.

**Funds Flow Agreement.** The parties shall negotiate and execute a funds flow agreement (the \"Funds Flow Agreement\") at least two (2) business days prior to the Closing Date, setting forth the exact dollar amounts and wire transfer instructions for all payments to be made at the Closing, including, without limitation: (a) repayment of all Target Indebtedness, (b) payment of all Seller Transaction Expenses, (c) deposit of the Escrow Amount with Pinnacle Trust Company, and (d) payment of the balance of the Purchase Price (after giving effect to the foregoing deductions) to Seller.

**Condition to Closing.** Delivery of payoff letters as described above shall be a condition to Buyer\'s obligation to consummate the Closing. In the event Seller fails to deliver any required payoff letter within the timeframe specified above, Buyer shall have the right, in its sole discretion, to (x) waive such condition and proceed with the Closing, or (y) delay the Closing until such payoff letter is delivered, subject to the Outside Date.
**[Section 7: Representations and Warranties]{.underline}**

**Seller\'s Representations and Warranties.** Seller shall make customary representations and warranties in the Definitive Agreement regarding Seller\'s authority to execute and deliver the Definitive Agreement and consummate the transactions contemplated thereby, the enforceability of the Definitive Agreement against Seller, Seller\'s valid title to the Shares (free and clear of all liens and encumbrances), and the absence of conflicts with Seller\'s organizational documents, material contracts, and applicable law (collectively, the \"Fundamental Representations\").

**Company Representations and Warranties.** The Definitive Agreement shall contain representations and warranties relating to the Company, which shall include, without limitation, representations regarding: organization and good standing; capitalization; financial statements (including the audited financial statements of the Company for the fiscal years ended December 31, 2022, 2023, and 2024); absence of undisclosed liabilities; compliance with applicable laws and regulations; environmental matters (including, without limitation, environmental permits, environmental liabilities, compliance with CERCLA and other environmental laws, and the use, storage, treatment, and disposal of hazardous materials); material contracts; intellectual property; employee and labor matters (including benefit plans); tax matters; owned and leased real property; insurance coverage; government contracts and compliance; and the absence of any Material Adverse Effect since December 31, 2024. The specific scope, detail, and materiality qualifiers applicable to each representation and warranty shall be negotiated and set forth in the Definitive Agreement, subject to the indemnification and survival terms set forth in this Term Sheet.

**Buyer\'s Representations and Warranties.** Buyer shall make customary representations and warranties in the Definitive Agreement regarding Buyer\'s authority, enforceability of the Definitive Agreement against Buyer, and the sufficiency of Buyer\'s financing to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby.
**[Section 8: Indemnification]{.underline}**

**Seller\'s Indemnification Obligations.** Seller shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Buyer and its affiliates (including, following the Closing, the Company and its subsidiaries), and their respective officers, directors, managers, members, employees, agents, and representatives (collectively, the \"Buyer Indemnified Parties\") from and against any and all losses, damages, liabilities, claims, demands, judgments, settlements, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and expenses) (collectively, \"Losses\") arising from, relating to, or in connection with: (i) any breach of or inaccuracy in any of Seller\'s representations and warranties contained in the Definitive Agreement, (ii) any breach of or failure to perform any of Seller\'s covenants or agreements contained in the Definitive Agreement, and (iii) the Special Indemnities described in Section 9 of this Term Sheet.

**General Indemnification Cap.** Seller\'s aggregate indemnification liability for Losses arising from breaches of non-Fundamental Representations shall not exceed twelve and one-half percent (12.5%) of the Base Enterprise Value, which equals Twenty-Six Million Eight Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$26,875,000) (\$215,000,000 × 0.125 = \$26,875,000) (the \"General Cap\"). For the avoidance of doubt, the parties have agreed that the general indemnification cap shall be twelve and one-half percent (12.5%) of the Base Enterprise Value.

**Fundamental Representations Cap.** Seller\'s aggregate indemnification liability for Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations shall not exceed the Purchase Price (as finally determined following completion of the post-closing true-up process described in Section 3).

**Basket (True Deductible).** Buyer shall not be entitled to indemnification for Losses arising from breaches of non-Fundamental Representations until the aggregate amount of such Losses exceeds one percent (1.0%) of the Base Enterprise Value, which equals Two Million One Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$2,150,000) (\$215,000,000 × 0.01 = \$2,150,000) (the \"Deductible\"). Once the aggregate amount of such Losses exceeds the Deductible, Buyer shall be entitled to indemnification only for Losses in excess of the Deductible (i.e., the basket shall operate as a true deductible, not a tipping basket or first-dollar basket). The Deductible shall not apply to Losses arising from (a) breaches of Fundamental Representations, (b) the Special Indemnities described in Section 9, or (c) claims arising from fraud or willful misconduct.
**Survival Periods.** The representations and warranties contained in the Definitive Agreement shall survive the Closing for the following periods:
> \(a\) *Fundamental Representations:* Fundamental Representations shall survive the Closing until the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations plus sixty (60) days.

> \(b\) *Non-Fundamental Representations (General):* Non-Fundamental Representations (other than environmental representations) shall survive the Closing for a period of eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date.

> \(c\) *Environmental Representations:* The survival period for environmental representations and warranties shall be negotiated and set forth in the Definitive Agreement, but shall in no event be less than thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date. Buyer reserves the right to seek survival of environmental representations through the full applicable statute of limitations.
> \(d\) *Covenants:* Covenants shall survive for the applicable performance period plus twelve (12) months, or such longer period as may be specified in the Definitive Agreement.
> \(e\) *Special Indemnities:* The survival period for the Special Indemnities shall be as set forth in Section 9 below.

**Sole Remedy.** Indemnification as set forth in the Definitive Agreement shall be the sole and exclusive post-Closing remedy of the parties for any breach of or inaccuracy in any representation or warranty contained in the Definitive Agreement, other than in the case of actual fraud or willful misconduct. Nothing in this Section 8 or in the Definitive Agreement shall limit any party\'s right to seek equitable relief, including specific performance and injunctive relief, as may be available at law or in equity.
**Escrow as Source of Recovery.** The Escrow Amount shall serve as a source of recovery for indemnification claims as described in Section 4 of this Term Sheet.
**[Section 9: Special Indemnity --- Dalton Creek CERCLA Matter]{.underline}**

**Dalton Creek Special Indemnity.** In addition to, and not subject to the limitations set forth in, the general indemnification provisions described in Section 8 above, Seller shall provide a special indemnity (the \"Dalton Creek Special Indemnity\") with respect to all Losses arising from, related to, or in connection with:

> \(i\) the pending information request from the United States Environmental Protection Agency (\"EPA\") under Section 104(e) of the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act, as amended (\"CERCLA\"), regarding the Company\'s former operations at the Dalton Creek disposal facility located in Clackamas County, Oregon (the \"Dalton Creek Facility\");

> \(ii\) any enforcement action, claim, investigation, order, consent decree, administrative order, or proceeding by any Governmental Authority or any third party relating to or arising out of the Company\'s operations, activities, or waste disposal practices at the Dalton Creek Facility; and

> \(iii\) any environmental contamination, remediation obligations, natural resource damages, response costs, or other liabilities associated with the Company\'s former operations at the Dalton Creek Facility, whether arising under CERCLA, the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act, the Oregon Environmental Cleanup Law, or any other federal, state, or local environmental law.

**Not Subject to Basket or Cap.** The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall not be subject to the Deductible or the General Cap set forth in Section 8 above. The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall be in addition to, and not in limitation of, Seller\'s other indemnification obligations under the Definitive Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, Losses indemnifiable under the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall not be counted toward, or reduce, the General Cap or the Deductible.
**Survival.** The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall survive the Closing for a period of seventy-two (72) months (six (6) years) following the Closing Date.

**Escrow Holdback.** A portion of the Escrow Amount shall be available to satisfy claims under the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, with such portion held for thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date, as set forth in Section 4 above. For the avoidance of doubt, Buyer\'s right to recover under the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall not be limited to the Escrow Amount, and Buyer shall be entitled to pursue claims against Seller directly for any Losses in excess of the available escrow funds.

**Background.** For reference, Seller has disclosed to Buyer the pending EPA information request under CERCLA Section 104(e) relating to the Dalton Creek Facility. Outside environmental counsel retained by the Company, Haverford Environmental Law Group, has estimated the Company\'s potential liability in connection with the Dalton Creek matter to be in the range of One Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$1,500,000) to Six Million Dollars (\$6,000,000). The Company maintains an environmental impairment liability insurance policy with Northshore Specialty Insurance Co. (Policy No. EIL-2024-0093712), with an aggregate limit of Fifteen Million Dollars (\$15,000,000) and a per-occurrence limit of Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000). The Definitive Agreement shall include provisions regarding the maintenance and application of such insurance coverage.
**[Section 10: Representations and Warranties Insurance]{.underline}**

**R&W Insurance Policy.** Buyer intends to obtain a representations and warranties insurance policy (the \"R&W Insurance Policy\") from Granite Ridge Underwriters (or such other insurer as Buyer may select in its sole discretion) in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Term Sheet and the Definitive Agreement. The cost of the R&W Insurance Policy (including all premiums, underwriting fees, broker fees, taxes, and other amounts payable in connection with the placement of such policy) shall be borne solely by Buyer. Buyer shall use commercially reasonable efforts to bind the R&W Insurance Policy on or prior to the Closing Date.

**Subrogation Waiver.** The Definitive Agreement shall include a provision pursuant to which Buyer agrees, and shall cause the R&W Insurance carrier to agree, that the R&W Insurance carrier shall waive, and shall not exercise, any right of subrogation against Seller or any of Seller\'s affiliates, officers, directors, employees, agents, or representatives with respect to any claim made under the R&W Insurance Policy, except in the case of actual fraud by Seller. This subrogation waiver shall survive the Closing and shall be included as a covenant of Buyer in the Definitive Agreement.

**Cooperation.** Seller shall, and shall cause the Company to, reasonably cooperate with Buyer and the R&W Insurance carrier in connection with the underwriting and placement of the R&W Insurance Policy. Such cooperation shall include, without limitation, (a) providing access to the Company\'s management team, including Patricia Huang and Robert Merrill, for underwriting interviews, (b) making available such documents, data, reports, and other information as may be reasonably requested by the R&W Insurance carrier in connection with its underwriting review, and (c) responding in a timely manner to reasonable follow-up inquiries from the R&W Insurance carrier. Seller\'s cooperation obligations under this Section 10 shall not require Seller to incur any unreasonable out-of-pocket expense (other than de minimis costs) without Buyer\'s prior agreement to reimburse such expense.
**[Section 11: Non-Competition; Non-Solicitation]{.underline}**

**Non-Competition.** The Definitive Agreement shall include a covenant pursuant to which Seller and its controlled affiliates shall agree not to, directly or indirectly, engage in, own, manage, operate, finance, control, or participate in the ownership, management, operation, or control of any business engaged in the provision of environmental remediation services or hazardous waste management services, subject to the following parameters:
> \(a\) *Duration:* Three (3) years following the Closing Date.
> \(b\) *Geographic Scope:* The States of Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada.
> \(c\) *Business Scope:* Environmental remediation services and hazardous waste management services, as such services are conducted by the Company as of the Closing Date.

> \(d\) *Bound Parties:* Seller and its controlled affiliates. For the avoidance of doubt, the non-competition covenant shall not apply to any portfolio company or operating subsidiary of Seller that is not engaged in environmental remediation or hazardous waste management as of the Closing Date.
**Carve-Outs.** The non-competition covenant shall not restrict Seller or its affiliates from:
> \(i\) conducting their existing construction and timber operations, as such operations are conducted as of the Closing Date;
> \(ii\) holding passive investments of less than five percent (5%) of the outstanding equity securities of any publicly traded entity; or

> \(iii\) performing environmental-related activities that are incidental to and performed solely in connection with Seller\'s construction or timber operations (e.g., erosion control, stormwater management, and environmental compliance activities performed on Seller\'s own construction or timber sites).

**Non-Solicitation.** The Definitive Agreement shall include a covenant pursuant to which Seller and its affiliates shall agree not to, directly or indirectly, for a period of two (2) years following the Closing Date, solicit, recruit, hire, or engage any individual who is an employee of the Company as of the Closing Date, or induce, encourage, or attempt to induce or encourage any such employee to terminate his or her employment with the Company. The non-solicitation covenant shall contain customary carve-outs for (a) general solicitations of employment (including through advertisements, job postings, or use of recruiting firms) that are not specifically directed at or targeted toward employees of the Company, and (b) the hiring of any employee of the Company who contacts Seller or its affiliates on his or her own initiative without any solicitation by or on behalf of Seller or its affiliates.

**Reasonableness.** The parties acknowledge and agree that the scope, duration, and geographic limitations of the non-competition and non-solicitation covenants set forth in this Section 11 are reasonable and necessary to protect the legitimate business interests of Buyer and the Company, and that Seller has received adequate consideration for such covenants in the form of the Purchase Price and the Earnout Payment.
**[Section 12: Key Closing Conditions]{.underline}**
**Mutual Conditions.** The obligations of both Buyer and Seller to consummate the Closing shall be subject to the satisfaction or waiver of each of the following conditions:
> \(a\) The applicable waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended (the \"HSR Act\"), shall have expired or been terminated.

> \(b\) No Governmental Authority shall have issued any order, injunction, decree, or ruling, and no law or regulation shall have been enacted, that prohibits or restrains the consummation of the Closing.
**Buyer\'s Conditions.** The obligation of Buyer to consummate the Closing shall be subject to the satisfaction or waiver of each of the following additional conditions:

> \(a\) The representations and warranties of Seller contained in the Definitive Agreement shall be true and correct in all material respects (or, in the case of representations and warranties qualified by materiality or Material Adverse Effect, in all respects) as of the date of the Definitive Agreement and as of the Closing Date, as if made on and as of such date (except for representations and warranties that speak as of a specific date, which shall be true and correct as of such date).

> \(b\) Seller shall have complied with and performed in all material respects all of the covenants and agreements required to be performed by Seller under the Definitive Agreement on or prior to the Closing Date.
> \(c\) No Material Adverse Effect shall have occurred since the date of the Definitive Agreement.
> \(d\) Seller shall have delivered to Buyer the executed payoff letters from each holder of Target Indebtedness as described in Section 6 of this Term Sheet.

> \(e\) Seller shall have delivered to Buyer a fully executed employment agreement between the Company and Patricia Huang (Chief Executive Officer) in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to Buyer.
> \(f\) Seller shall have delivered to Buyer the Escrow Agreement, duly executed by Seller and Pinnacle Trust Company.
> \(g\) Buyer shall have received all third-party consents listed on a schedule to the Definitive Agreement, in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to Buyer.

> \(h\) Seller shall have delivered certificates of good standing (or equivalent) for the Company from the Oregon Secretary of State and from the Secretary of State of each other jurisdiction in which the Company is qualified to do business, each dated within ten (10) business days of the Closing Date.
> \(i\) Such other customary closing conditions as shall be set forth in the Definitive Agreement.
**Seller\'s Conditions.** The obligation of Seller to consummate the Closing shall be subject to the satisfaction or waiver of each of the following additional conditions:

> \(a\) The representations and warranties of Buyer contained in the Definitive Agreement shall be true and correct in all material respects as of the date of the Definitive Agreement and as of the Closing Date.

> \(b\) Buyer shall have complied with and performed in all material respects all of the covenants and agreements required to be performed by Buyer under the Definitive Agreement on or prior to the Closing Date.

> \(c\) Buyer shall have delivered to Seller the Purchase Price (less amounts deposited in escrow, amounts paid to retire Target Indebtedness, and amounts paid in respect of Seller Transaction Expenses) in immediately available funds by wire transfer to the account(s) designated by Seller.
**[Section 13: Covenants]{.underline}**
**Pre-Closing Covenants.** The Definitive Agreement shall include customary pre-closing covenants, including but not limited to:

> \(a\) *Ordinary Course of Business:* Seller shall cause the Company to operate its business in the ordinary course consistent with past practice between the date of the Definitive Agreement and the Closing Date.

> \(b\) *Access:* Seller shall provide Buyer and its representatives with reasonable access to the Company\'s books, records, properties, contracts, and personnel during normal business hours and upon reasonable advance notice, subject to applicable law and the preservation of attorney-client privilege.

> \(c\) *HSR Act Filing:* The parties shall file all required notifications under the HSR Act within ten (10) business days following execution of the Definitive Agreement and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain early termination of the applicable waiting period.

> \(d\) *Third-Party Consents:* Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain all third-party consents required in connection with the transactions contemplated by the Definitive Agreement.

> \(e\) *Financing Cooperation:* Seller shall, and shall cause the Company to, reasonably cooperate with Buyer in connection with Buyer\'s debt financing commitment from Clearwater Environmental Lending Corp., including providing financial information, participating in lender meetings, and facilitating collateral diligence, in each case to the extent reasonably requested by Buyer.
> \(f\) *R&W Insurance Cooperation:* Seller shall cooperate with Buyer in connection with the underwriting and placement of the R&W Insurance Policy, as described in Section 10 of this Term Sheet.

> \(g\) *Interim Operating Restrictions:* The Definitive Agreement shall include specific interim covenants restricting the Company from taking certain significant actions without Buyer\'s prior written consent, including but not limited to: incurring capital expenditures in excess of agreed thresholds, incurring or assuming additional indebtedness, issuing equity, entering into or materially amending material contracts, making material changes to employee compensation or benefits, settling material litigation, or disposing of material assets.
**Post-Closing Covenants.** The Definitive Agreement shall include the following post-closing covenants:
> \(a\) *Non-Competition and Non-Solicitation:* As described in Section 11 of this Term Sheet.

> \(b\) *Tax Cooperation:* The parties shall cooperate in the preparation and filing of all tax returns and in the resolution of any tax audits, assessments, or disputes relating to the Company for any pre-closing tax period.

> \(c\) *Books and Records:* Buyer shall provide Seller with reasonable access to the books and records of the Company relating to pre-closing periods for a period of seven (7) years following the Closing Date.

> \(d\) *Further Assurances:* Each party shall, from time to time following the Closing, execute and deliver such additional documents and instruments and take such further actions as may be reasonably necessary to effectuate the transactions contemplated hereby.
**[Section 14: Termination]{.underline}**

**Outside Date.** Either party may terminate this Term Sheet and the obligations of the parties hereunder (and, following execution, the Definitive Agreement) if the Closing has not occurred on or before February 28, 2026 (the \"Outside Date\"); provided, however, that the right to terminate shall not be available to any party whose material breach of this Term Sheet (or, following execution, the Definitive Agreement) has been the primary cause of the failure of the Closing to occur by the Outside Date.
**Mutual Termination.** This Term Sheet (and, following execution, the Definitive Agreement) may be terminated at any time by the mutual written agreement of Buyer and Seller.

**Governmental Prohibition.** Either party may terminate this Term Sheet (and, following execution, the Definitive Agreement) if any Governmental Authority of competent jurisdiction shall have issued a final, non-appealable order, decree, or ruling permanently prohibiting or enjoining the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby.
**No Termination Fees.** No termination fee, reverse termination fee, or break-up fee shall be payable by either party upon the termination of this Term Sheet or the Definitive Agreement.
**[Section 15: Financing]{.underline}**

Buyer has obtained a commitment letter, dated September 3, 2025, from Clearwater Environmental Lending Corp. for a senior secured credit facility in an aggregate principal amount of up to One Hundred Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$125,000,000) (the \"Financing Commitment\") to be used, in part, to fund the Purchase Price and the other transactions contemplated by this Term Sheet. Buyer shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain the Financing Commitment in full force and effect and to satisfy all conditions under the Financing Commitment. The availability of financing from Clearwater Environmental Lending Corp. or any other source is not a condition to Buyer\'s obligation to consummate the Closing. Buyer represents that it has, or will have at the Closing, sufficient funds (including the proceeds of the Financing Commitment, together with Buyer\'s available cash on hand and other committed capital) to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby and to pay the Purchase Price and all other amounts required to be paid by Buyer hereunder and under the Definitive Agreement.
**[Section 16: Advisors]{.underline}**
The following advisors are engaged by the respective parties in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Term Sheet:
**Buyer\'s Counsel:** Ashford, Pennington & Yates LLP; Lead Partner: Elena Vasquez-Moreno; 71 South Wacker Drive, Suite 4500, Chicago, Illinois 60606.
**Seller\'s Counsel:** Fortuna & Blake LLP; Lead Partner: Douglas Renwick; 900 SW Fifth Avenue, Suite 2400, Portland, Oregon 97204.
**Buyer\'s Financial Advisor:** Ridgeline Advisors LLC.
**Target\'s Independent Auditor:** Winslow & Tate CPA Group.

Each party shall be responsible for its own advisory fees and expenses incurred in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Term Sheet and the Definitive Agreement; provided, however, that Seller Transaction Expenses (as defined herein) shall be paid from the Purchase Price at the Closing in accordance with the funds flow mechanics described in Sections 3 and 6 of this Term Sheet.
**[Section 17: Exclusivity; Confidentiality]{.underline}**

**Exclusivity.** From the date of this Term Sheet through the earlier of (i) the execution and delivery of the Definitive Agreement by all parties thereto, (ii) the valid termination of this Term Sheet in accordance with Section 14, or (iii) November 30, 2025, Seller shall not, and shall cause the Company and its respective directors, officers, employees, agents, and representatives not to, directly or indirectly, (a) solicit, initiate, encourage, or facilitate any inquiry, proposal, or offer from any third party relating to any acquisition of all or a material portion of the equity interests or assets of the Company, (b) enter into or participate in any discussions or negotiations with any third party regarding any such acquisition, or (c) provide any non-public information to any third party in connection with any such acquisition. Seller shall promptly notify Buyer in writing of any unsolicited inquiry, proposal, or offer received by Seller, the Company, or any of their respective representatives during the exclusivity period.

**Confidentiality.** The terms and conditions of this Term Sheet and the transactions contemplated hereby shall remain subject to that certain Confidentiality Agreement dated July 12, 2025 between Buyer and Seller (the \"Confidentiality Agreement\"), which is hereby incorporated by reference. The parties acknowledge and agree that this Term Sheet constitutes \"Confidential Information\" under the Confidentiality Agreement.
**[Section 18: Binding Provisions; Governing Law]{.underline}**
**Binding Effect.** This Term Sheet shall be binding on the parties with respect to the following provisions:
> \(i\) Section 17 (Exclusivity; Confidentiality);
> \(ii\) This Section 18 (Binding Provisions; Governing Law);
> \(iii\) Section 3 (Purchase Price), solely as to the Base Enterprise Value and the purchase price formula set forth therein;

> \(iv\) Section 8 (Indemnification), solely as to the general indemnification cap percentage (12.5% of the Base Enterprise Value), the basket type (true deductible) and percentage (1.0% of the Base Enterprise Value), and the Special Indemnity terms set forth in Section 9;
> \(v\) Section 11 (Non-Competition; Non-Solicitation), as to the scope, duration, geographic limitations, and carve-outs set forth therein; and
> \(vi\) Section 6 (Closing Indebtedness Payoff Mechanics), as to the requirement for payoff letters and simultaneous closing payoff through the closing funds flow.

All other terms and conditions set forth in this Term Sheet are subject to negotiation and documentation in the Definitive Agreement; provided, however, that the parties shall negotiate in good faith to finalize and execute a Definitive Agreement that is consistent in all material respects with the terms set forth herein. Neither party shall unreasonably withhold, delay, or condition its agreement to terms in the Definitive Agreement that are consistent with this Term Sheet.

**Governing Law.** This Term Sheet shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to the conflicts of law principles thereof that would require the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.

**Dispute Resolution.** Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to this Term Sheet, including any question regarding its existence, validity, interpretation, breach, or termination, shall be resolved by binding arbitration administered by JAMS in Chicago, Illinois, in accordance with the JAMS Comprehensive Arbitration Rules and Procedures then in effect. The arbitration shall be conducted by a single arbitrator mutually selected by the parties (or, if the parties are unable to agree, appointed by JAMS). The decision of the arbitrator shall be final and binding on the parties, and judgment upon the award rendered by the arbitrator may be entered in any court having jurisdiction thereof.

**Amendments.** This Term Sheet may be amended, modified, or supplemented only by a written instrument signed by each of the parties hereto. No waiver of any provision of this Term Sheet shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought.

**Counterparts.** This Term Sheet may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Signatures delivered by electronic transmission (including by portable document format (.pdf), DocuSign, or other electronic signature technology) shall be deemed original signatures and shall be binding on the party providing such signature with the same force and effect as if such signatures were original ink signatures.
**[Section 19: Target Signing and Closing Timeline]{.underline}**

The parties shall use commercially reasonable efforts to finalize, negotiate, and execute the Definitive Agreement on or before November 14, 2025. The Closing of the transactions contemplated by this Term Sheet and the Definitive Agreement (the \"Closing\") is expected to occur approximately sixty (60) to seventy-five (75) days following execution of the Definitive Agreement, subject to the satisfaction or waiver of all applicable closing conditions (estimated target: mid-January 2026). The Outside Date for the Closing shall be February 28, 2026, as set forth in Section 14 of this Term Sheet.
**[Section 20: Notices]{.underline}**

All notices, requests, demands, consents, and other communications required or permitted under this Term Sheet shall be in writing and shall be deemed duly given when delivered personally, when sent by email (with confirmation of receipt), or when sent by nationally recognized overnight courier, addressed as follows:

> Email: evasquez-moreno@apylaw.com
**If to Seller:**
> Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc. 1550 NW Everett Street, Suite 800 Portland, Oregon 97209
> Attention: Harold T. Lindquist, Chief Executive Officer
> Email: hlindquist@evergreenholdings.com
> with a copy (which shall not constitute notice) to:

> Email: drenwick@fortunablake.com
Either party may change its address or other contact information for notices by providing written notice of such change to the other party in accordance with this Section 20.

21: Ashford, Pennington & Yates LLP\'s Environmental Practice Group has completed its environmental due diligence review of Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc. (\"Cascadia\" or the \"Company\"), an Oregon corporation headquartered at 8700 SW Tualatin-Sherwood Road, Suite 200, Tualatin, Oregon 97062. 63: **[III. Dalton Creek Disposal Facility --- CERCLA Exposure]{.underline}**
64: 
65: **[A. Background]{.underline}**
66: 
67: Cascadia formerly operated at the Dalton Creek disposal facility, a former hazardous waste disposal site located in Clackamas County, Oregon. The Company\'s operations at Dalton Creek involved the handling, treatment, and disposal of hazardous wastes generated by third-party industrial customers. These operations significantly predate the current management team and were conducted during a period when the Company was under different operational leadership. According to records produced during due diligence and confirmed by management interviews, Cascadia ceased all operations at the Dalton Creek disposal facility in approximately 2015.
68: 
69: In February 2025, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Region 10, issued an information request to Cascadia under Section 104(e) of the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980, as amended (\"CERCLA\"), 42 U.S.C. § 9604(e). The information request seeks comprehensive documentation of the Company\'s waste handling and disposal activities at the Dalton Creek facility, including waste manifests, disposal records, volume and characterization data, and operational history during the period of the Company\'s use of the site.
70: 
71: As of the date of this memorandum, no formal enforcement action, notice of potential responsible party (\"PRP\") designation, unilateral administrative order, or lawsuit has been filed or issued by EPA or any other party against Cascadia in connection with the Dalton Creek facility. However, the issuance of a § 104(e) information request is widely recognized as a standard precursor to potential PRP designation and subsequent enforcement activity under CERCLA. The Company\'s management confirmed that it has retained outside environmental counsel to assist with the response to the information request and to monitor developments at the site.
72: 
73: **[B. Estimated Liability Exposure]{.underline}**
74: 
75: Based on our review of the Company\'s records, the EPA information request and the Company\'s response, publicly available site information, and consultation with environmental counsel experienced in CERCLA cost allocation proceedings, we estimate Cascadia\'s potential liability exposure in connection with the Dalton Creek disposal facility to be in the range of **\$1,500,000 to \$6,000,000**. The factors underlying this range are as follows:
76: 
77: > • **Low End (\$1,500,000).** This estimate assumes that EPA pursues a multi-party cost allocation among all identified potentially responsible parties at the Dalton Creek site, that Cascadia\'s proportionate share of total cleanup costs is determined on the basis of the volume and toxicity of waste it disposed at the facility, and that other identified PRPs remain solvent and capable of bearing their respective shares. Under this scenario, Cascadia\'s share would represent a minority allocation consistent with its relative contribution to site contamination.
78: >
79: > • **High End (\$6,000,000).** This estimate reflects the possibility that EPA may designate Cascadia as a major contributor to the contamination at the site, or that one or more other PRPs may prove financially unable to satisfy their allocated shares. Under CERCLA § 107, liability is joint and several, meaning that EPA may seek recovery of the full cost of remediation from any single PRP, regardless of that party\'s proportionate contribution. If other PRPs are insolvent or unidentifiable, Cascadia\'s exposure could increase significantly. The high-end estimate also accounts for the possibility that the overall scope and cost of site remediation may exceed current projections.
80: 
81: It is important to note that CERCLA proceedings frequently extend over many years. Under CERCLA § 113(g)(2), the statute of limitations for a cost recovery action is six years from the date of completion of a remedial action at the site. Contribution claims under § 113(f) may extend further depending on the timing of settlement or judgment. Given that no formal remedial action has been initiated at the Dalton Creek site, it is possible that Cascadia\'s ultimate liability will not be determined for a period of years following the closing of the proposed transaction.
82: 
83: The Company\'s environmental impairment liability insurance with Northshore Specialty Insurance Co. (aggregate limit \$15,000,000; per-occurrence limit \$5,000,000) may provide coverage for defense costs and some portion of the Company\'s ultimate liability in connection with the Dalton Creek matter. However, coverage for legacy disposal operations is commonly subject to policy exclusions, including prior-knowledge exclusions, pollution date restrictions, and exclusions for known or disclosed conditions. We recommend that insurance counsel conduct a detailed review of the applicable policy terms to determine the extent and reliability of available coverage.
84: 
85: **[C. SPA Recommendations --- Dalton Creek]{.underline}**
86: 
87: Based on the foregoing analysis, we make the following recommendations with respect to the treatment of the Dalton Creek CERCLA exposure in the Stock Purchase Agreement:
88: 
89: **Recommendation 1 --- Special Indemnity.** Given the magnitude of the potential exposure (\$1,500,000 to \$6,000,000), the fact that this is a known and disclosed environmental liability arising from Seller\'s period of ownership, and the inherent uncertainty and protracted timeline of CERCLA proceedings, we **strongly recommend** that the SPA include a **Special Indemnity** obligating Seller to indemnify Buyer for all Losses arising from or related to the Dalton Creek disposal facility and the EPA\'s CERCLA § 104(e) information request, including without limitation all costs of investigation, remediation, defense, settlement, contribution, and related administrative proceedings. The Special Indemnity should be structured as follows:
90: 
91: > \(a\) **Survival Period.** The Special Indemnity should survive for no less than **72 months** following the closing date, in order to account for the characteristically lengthy timeline of CERCLA proceedings and the six-year statute of limitations for CERCLA cost recovery actions under § 113(g)(2). A shorter survival period would create an unacceptable risk that Buyer\'s indemnification rights expire before a formal CERCLA claim crystallizes.
92: >
93: > \(b\) **Exclusion from General Basket and Cap.** The Special Indemnity should **not** be subject to the general indemnification deductible basket or aggregate liability cap. The Dalton Creek matter is a known, quantifiable exposure that should be indemnified on a dollar-for-dollar basis from the first dollar of Loss. Subjecting this exposure to general basket and cap limitations would improperly shift a portion of the known risk to Buyer.
94: >
95: > \(c\) **Escrow Holdback.** The Special Indemnity should be supported by a dedicated portion of the **escrow holdback** maintained with Pinnacle Trust Company for a minimum period of **36 months** following closing. The escrowed amount should be sufficient to cover at least the low end of the estimated liability range (\$1,500,000), with the full Special Indemnity obligation surviving for the 72-month period regardless of the release of escrowed funds.
96: >
97: > \(d\) **Consistency with Term Sheet.** We note that the executed term sheet dated September 10, 2025, between Whitmore Capital Partners LLC and Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc., specifically provides for a \"Special Indemnity\" to address the Dalton Creek matter. The SPA must implement this agreed-upon commercial term. Omission of the Special Indemnity from the Seller\'s initial SPA draft would represent a departure from the agreed deal terms.
98: 
99: **Recommendation 2 --- Extended Survival of Environmental Representations.** Independent of and in addition to the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, the environmental representations and warranties in the SPA should survive for a minimum of **36 months** post-closing, and ideally for the **full applicable statute of limitations** for environmental claims. We understand that seller-favorable first drafts in the middle market typically propose a 12-month survival period for representations and warranties, including environmental representations. For a company whose core business is the provision of environmental remediation and hazardous waste management services, a 12-month survival period for environmental representations would be wholly inadequate for the following reasons:
100: 
101: > \(a\) The Dalton Creek CERCLA exposure may not crystallize into a formal claim, enforcement action, or PRP designation for a period of years following closing, as discussed in Section III.B above.
102: >
103: > \(b\) Cascadia\'s active remediation projects, including the Hargrove Industrial Site project, have multi-year performance timelines during which new environmental liabilities or breaches of environmental representations may emerge.
104: >
105: > \(c\) Environmental liabilities in the remediation services sector routinely emerge well beyond a 12-month period due to the nature of contamination migration, delayed regulatory action, and evolving site characterization data.
106: >
107: > \(d\) For a company whose entire value proposition is built upon environmental compliance and permitting, the environmental representations are among the most critical representations in the agreement and should be afforded extended protection commensurate with that importance.
108: 
109: We recommend that the deal team take a firm position on extended survival of environmental representations during SPA negotiations.

143: **[B. Change-of-Control Transfer and Notification Requirements]{.underline}**
144: 
145: Although this transaction is structured as a **stock purchase** --- and therefore the legal entity holding the permits (Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc.) will not change --- many state environmental regulatory programs nonetheless require **notification to or approval from the issuing agency** upon a change in the ownership or control of the permit holder. This is a critical issue that must be addressed in the SPA. The applicable state-specific requirements include:
146: 
147: > • **Oregon.** Oregon DEQ regulations require notification of a change of ownership or control of a permitted facility within 30 days of such change. Certain RCRA permits issued by Oregon DEQ may require formal transfer approval prior to the change taking effect. *See* OAR Chapter 340, Division 012 and applicable permit conditions.
148: >
149: > • **Washington.** The Washington Department of Ecology requires prior written notification for changes in control of permitted entities. Certain permits include conditions that expressly require agency approval of ownership changes before the transfer is deemed valid. *See* WAC Chapter 173-303 and applicable permit conditions.
150: >
151: > • **California.** The California Department of Toxic Substances Control (\"DTSC\") and regional water quality control boards often require notification and, in certain permit categories, prior approval for changes in control of entities holding hazardous waste facility permits and waste discharge requirements. The specific requirements vary by permit type and issuing authority.
152: >
153: > • **Nevada.** The Nevada Division of Environmental Protection requires notification of ownership changes for certain categories of environmental permits, including hazardous waste management permits and water pollution control permits.
154: 
155: Even in a stock acquisition, these agencies may treat a change of the ultimate parent company --- here, the acquisition of Cascadia\'s shares by Whitmore Capital Partners LLC from Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc. --- as a \"change of ownership or control\" that triggers notification or approval requirements under the applicable permit or regulation. Failure to comply with these requirements could result in permit violations, enforcement actions, fines, or in extreme cases, permit revocation or suspension. Given that Cascadia\'s business is entirely dependent upon its ability to perform work under these permits, any disruption to the permit portfolio would be material.

However, a mere representation regarding the current status of permits is insufficient to protect Buyer from the risks associated with the change-of-control process. We **strongly recommend** that the SPA include the following provisions:

159: > \(a\) **Pre-Closing Covenant.** A covenant requiring Seller and the Company, prior to closing, to (i) identify all environmental permits that require change-of-control notification to or approval from the issuing agency, (ii) prepare and submit all required notifications and applications for approval to the appropriate state environmental agencies, and (iii) cooperate with Buyer in providing all information reasonably requested by any such agency in connection with the change-of-control process.

161: > \(b\) **Post-Closing Cooperation Covenant.** A covenant obligating Seller to cooperate with Buyer following closing in completing any permit transfer, re-issuance, amendment, or notification process required by any governmental authority as a result of the change of control, including executing documents, providing historical information, and participating in agency proceedings as reasonably requested by Buyer.
162: >
163: > \(c\) **Survival.** These covenants should survive closing for at least **12 months**, or such longer period as may be necessary to complete all pending permit transfers and notifications, including any pending agency review or approval processes.
164:

183: **[B. Anti-Assignment Act and FAR Novation Requirements]{.underline}**
184: 
185: Federal government contracts are subject to the **Anti-Assignment Act, 41 U.S.C. § 6305**, which generally prohibits the transfer or assignment of government contracts without the consent of the contracting officer. While the Anti-Assignment Act has historically been interpreted to apply primarily to assignments of the contract itself (as opposed to changes in corporate ownership), the **Federal Acquisition Regulation (\"FAR\"), Part 42, Subpart 42.12**, specifically addresses changes in the contractor\'s organizational structure, including changes in ownership.
186: 
187: Under **FAR 42.1204**, when a contractor undergoes a change in ownership --- including when a third party acquires the stock of the contractor --- the contractor is required to submit a request for a **novation agreement** (or, in some cases, a **change-of-name agreement**) to the responsible contracting officer. A novation agreement formally recognizes the successor entity and transfers the government\'s contractual rights and obligations to the recognized successor. The key requirements under FAR 42.12 include:
188: 
189: > • **FAR 42.1204(a).** The contractor must submit a written request for novation to the responsible contracting officer, accompanied by supporting documentation including the acquisition agreement (or relevant portions thereof), a list of all affected contracts, and evidence of the transferee\'s technical and financial capability to perform.
190: >
191: > • **FAR 42.1204(e).** The contracting officer must make an affirmative determination that recognizing the successor is in the government\'s interest before executing the novation agreement.
192: >
193: > • **Interim Period.** Until a novation agreement is executed, the government may continue to treat the original contractor as the responsible party under the contract. Failure to obtain novation could result in the government treating the change of ownership as a breach of the contract, potentially leading to termination for default or termination for convenience.
194: 
195: **For the two federal contracts** --- the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers contract and the Bureau of Land Management contract --- **novation agreements will be required** under FAR 42.12 because Whitmore Capital Partners LLC, a new parent entity with no prior relationship to Cascadia, is acquiring 100% of the outstanding stock of the Company from Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc.
196: 
197: **For the two state contracts** --- the Oregon DEQ contract and the Washington Department of Ecology contract --- analogous state procurement regulations may impose similar notification or approval requirements for changes in corporate ownership of a government contractor. The specific requirements depend on the terms of each contract and the applicable state procurement code. These state contracts require further review of their specific provisions and the relevant Oregon and Washington procurement regulations.
198: 
199: **Risk Assessment.** We assess this as a **HIGH RISK** item. Failure to obtain required novation agreements or government consents could result in **contract termination**, which would eliminate a material revenue stream, potentially trigger cross-default provisions under the Company\'s other contracts or financing arrangements, and materially impair the value of Buyer\'s investment. The novation process is not merely administrative --- contracting officers have discretion to deny novation if they determine that the successor entity does not have the capability or resources to perform, or if recognition is not in the government\'s interest.
200: 
201: **[C. SPA Recommendations --- Government Contracts]{.underline}**
202: 
203: Based on the foregoing analysis, we make the following recommendations:
204: 
205: **Recommendation 1 --- Pre-Closing Covenant.** The SPA should include a specific covenant requiring Seller and the Company to (a) promptly notify each government contracting officer (federal and state) of the contemplated transaction, (b) submit all required novation request packages under FAR 42.12 for the two federal contracts and all analogous submissions required under state procurement regulations for the two state contracts, and (c) use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain all required novation agreements, recognition agreements, or government consents prior to closing.
206: 
207: **Recommendation 2 --- Closing Condition or Specific Covenant.** The deal team should carefully consider whether to make completion of the government contract novation process a **condition to closing** or a **pre-closing best-efforts covenant with a post-closing cooperation tail**. Given that the FAR novation process can take 60 to 120 days or longer, requiring full novation completion as a hard closing condition could delay closing beyond the expected mid-January 2026 timeline or the February 28, 2026 outside date set forth in the term sheet. We recommend the following balanced approach:
208: 
209: > \(a\) Require that all novation requests and government notifications have been **submitted** to all relevant contracting officers prior to closing.
210: >
211: > \(b\) Require that no government contracting officer has **denied** a novation request or indicated an intent to terminate, suspend, or materially modify any government contract as a result of the contemplated transaction.
212: >
213: > \(c\) Include a **post-closing cooperation covenant** requiring Seller to continue cooperating in the novation process following closing, including executing documents, providing information, and participating in meetings with contracting officers as reasonably requested by Buyer.
214: 
215: **Recommendation 3 --- Representations.** The SPA should include specific representations that (a) Seller has provided complete and accurate copies of all government contracts, including all modifications, amendments, and task orders, (b) the Company is in material compliance with all terms of such government contracts, (c) no government contract is the subject of any pending or threatened termination, suspension, or debarment proceeding, and (d) to Seller\'s Knowledge, no contracting officer has indicated any intent to terminate, not renew, or materially modify any such contract.
216: 
217: **Recommendation 4 --- Risk Allocation.** If any government contract is terminated as a result of the change of ownership and the failure to obtain the required novation agreement or government consent, the resulting Losses --- including lost revenue, contract penalties, and consequential damages --- should be allocated to Seller through the indemnification provisions of the SPA.
218: 
219: We note that the Seller\'s SPA draft should be carefully reviewed to determine whether the conditions-to-closing article addresses government contract consents separately from general third-party consents. It is common in seller-favorable first drafts to group government contract consents with general commercial consents --- this approach is insufficient given the unique federal regulatory framework applicable to government contracts and the heightened risk of contract termination. Government contract novation should be treated as a distinct and specifically addressed closing requirement.

**PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL --- ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT** This memorandum is protected by the attorney-client privilege and the work product doctrine. It is intended solely for use by the attorneys and professionals of Ashford, Pennington & Yates LLP and the client to whom it is addressed.
