**[ARTICLE II]{.underline}**
**[PURCHASE AND SALE; PURCHASE PRICE]{.underline}**
**Section 2.01 Purchase and Sale of Shares**

Upon the terms and subject to the conditions of this Agreement, at the Closing, Seller shall sell, assign, transfer, convey, and deliver to Buyer, and Buyer shall purchase, acquire, and accept from Seller, all of the Shares, constituting 1,000,000 shares of common stock, par value \$0.01 per share, of the Company, which represent all of the issued and outstanding shares of capital stock of the Company, free and clear of all Encumbrances (other than restrictions arising under applicable securities Laws), for the Purchase Price, payable as provided in Sections 2.02 and 2.03.
**Section 2.02 Purchase Price**

The aggregate purchase price for the Shares (the \"Purchase Price\") shall be an amount equal to (a) the Base Enterprise Value (\$215,000,000), *plus* (b) the amount, if any, by which the Estimated Closing NWC exceeds the Target NWC, *minus* (c) the amount, if any, by which the Target NWC exceeds the Estimated Closing NWC, *minus* (d) the Estimated Closing Indebtedness, *minus* (e) the Estimated Transaction Expenses. For illustrative purposes only, based on preliminary estimates, the Purchase Price would be calculated as follows: \$215,000,000 + \$18,200,000 (Estimated Closing NWC at Target) -- \$42,300,000 (Estimated Closing Indebtedness) -- \$3,900,000 (Estimated Transaction Expenses) = \$187,000,000. The Purchase Price shall be subject to adjustment as provided in Sections 2.03 and 2.04. The Purchase Price does not include any Earnout Payment that may become payable pursuant to Section 2.05, which shall be in addition to the Purchase Price.
**Section 2.03 Closing Payment and Estimates**

**(a)** *Pre-Closing Estimate.* Not later than three (3) Business Days prior to the Closing Date, Seller shall prepare and deliver to Buyer a written statement (the \"Estimated Closing Statement\") setting forth Seller\'s good-faith estimates of: (i) the Closing NWC (the \"Estimated Closing NWC\"), (ii) the Closing Indebtedness (the \"Estimated Closing Indebtedness\"), and (iii) the Transaction Expenses (the \"Estimated Transaction Expenses\"), together with reasonable supporting documentation, schedules, and work papers used in the preparation thereof. The Estimated Closing Statement shall be prepared in accordance with the Accounting Principles and shall include a calculation of the estimated Purchase Price based on such estimates. Seller shall provide Buyer with reasonable access to the books and records of the Company and the work papers of the Company\'s accountants as Buyer may reasonably request to verify the Estimated Closing Statement. If Buyer delivers written notice of any objections to the Estimated Closing Statement within two (2) Business Days after receipt thereof, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith to resolve such objections prior to the Closing Date; *provided* that the failure of the Parties to resolve any such objections shall not delay the Closing, and the Estimated Closing Statement, as adjusted by mutual agreement of the Parties (or, absent such agreement, as originally delivered by Seller), shall be used for purposes of calculating the Closing Payment, subject to the post-Closing adjustment procedures set forth in Section 2.04.

**(b)** *Closing Payment.* At the Closing, Buyer shall pay to Seller an aggregate amount in cash (the \"Closing Payment\") equal to (i) the Purchase Price (calculated using the estimates set forth in the Estimated Closing Statement), *minus* (ii) the Escrow Amount (\$16,125,000). The Closing Payment shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to one or more bank accounts designated in writing by Seller to Buyer no later than two (2) Business Days prior to the Closing Date.

**(c)** *Escrow Deposit.* At the Closing, Buyer shall deposit the Escrow Amount, in cash, by wire transfer of immediately available funds, with the Escrow Agent in accordance with the terms of the Escrow Agreement. The Escrow Fund shall be held, invested, and disbursed by the Escrow Agent in accordance with the terms of the Escrow Agreement. The Escrow Fund shall serve as security for Seller\'s indemnification obligations under Article IX and the post-Closing adjustment obligations under Section 2.04, as and to the extent provided herein and in the Escrow Agreement.

**(d)** *Repayment of Closing Indebtedness.* At or promptly following the Closing, Buyer shall cause the Company to repay, discharge, and satisfy in full all Closing Indebtedness. Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cooperate with Buyer in connection with the repayment of such Closing Indebtedness.
**Section 2.04 Post-Closing NWC Adjustment**

**(a)** *Closing Statement.* Within ninety (90) days following the Closing Date, Buyer shall prepare and deliver to Seller a written statement (the \"Closing Statement\") setting forth Buyer\'s good-faith calculation of the actual (i) Closing NWC, (ii) Closing Indebtedness, and (iii) Transaction Expenses, together with reasonable supporting documentation, schedules, and work papers. The Closing Statement shall be prepared in accordance with the Accounting Principles and in a manner consistent with the preparation of the Estimated Closing Statement. Buyer shall provide Seller and its Representatives with reasonable access, during normal business hours and upon reasonable prior notice, to the books and records of the Company and the work papers used in the preparation of the Closing Statement.

**(b)** *Review and Objection.* Seller shall have thirty (30) days following receipt of the Closing Statement (the \"Review Period\") to review the Closing Statement. During the Review Period, Buyer shall provide Seller and its Representatives with reasonable access to the books and records of the Company, the work papers of the Company\'s accountants, and the personnel of the Company, in each case to the extent reasonably necessary for Seller\'s review of the Closing Statement. If Seller does not deliver a written notice of objection (an \"Objection Notice\") to Buyer within the Review Period, the Closing Statement as delivered by Buyer shall be deemed final and binding on the Parties. If Seller delivers an Objection Notice within the Review Period, such Objection Notice shall specify in reasonable detail each item in dispute (each, a \"Disputed Item\"), the basis for such dispute, and the amount Seller believes to be the correct amount. Any item or amount not specifically identified as a Disputed Item in the Objection Notice shall be deemed accepted by Seller and shall be final and binding on the Parties.

**(c)** *Resolution of Disputes.* If Seller delivers a timely Objection Notice, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith for a period of twenty (20) Business Days following delivery of the Objection Notice (the \"Resolution Period\") to resolve all Disputed Items. If the Parties are unable to resolve all Disputed Items within the Resolution Period, any remaining Disputed Items shall be submitted for final resolution to an independent, nationally recognized accounting firm mutually agreed upon by Buyer and Seller (the \"Independent Accountant\"); *provided* that such firm shall not be Winslow & Tate CPA Group, the auditors of the Company, or any accounting firm that has provided services to Buyer or Seller during the twenty-four (24) month period prior to such engagement. The Independent Accountant shall be engaged to resolve only the remaining Disputed Items and shall determine the correct amount of each such Disputed Item in accordance with the Accounting Principles, and such determination shall be final and binding on the Parties, absent manifest error. The Independent Accountant shall not assign a value to any Disputed Item that is greater than the highest value or less than the lowest value claimed by either Party. The Independent Accountant shall render its written determination within thirty (30) days after such engagement and shall set forth in such determination a reasoned basis for its resolution of each Disputed Item. The fees and expenses of the Independent Accountant shall be allocated between the Parties based on the relative amounts of the aggregate Disputed Items resolved in favor of each Party (as determined by the Independent Accountant), such that the Party whose positions are furthest from the Independent Accountant\'s determinations bears a proportionally greater share of such fees and expenses.
**(d)** *Adjustment Payment.* Within five (5) Business Days after the final determination of the Closing Statement (as determined pursuant to this Section 2.04):

> \(i\) If the Purchase Price as finally determined (using the actual Closing NWC, Closing Indebtedness, and Transaction Expenses as finally determined) exceeds the Purchase Price as calculated using the Estimated Closing Statement, Buyer shall pay such excess amount to Seller by wire transfer of immediately available funds.

> \(ii\) If the Purchase Price as calculated using the Estimated Closing Statement exceeds the Purchase Price as finally determined, Seller shall pay such excess amount to Buyer (first, by instructing the Escrow Agent to release such amount from the Escrow Fund, and, to the extent the Escrow Fund is insufficient, by wire transfer of immediately available funds from Seller directly to Buyer).

All adjustments pursuant to this Section 2.04 shall be made on a dollar-for-dollar basis from the first dollar of any difference, without any collar, threshold, or de minimis amount. Any adjustment amounts payable under this Section 2.04 shall bear interest from the Closing Date through the date of payment at the prime rate as published in *The Wall Street Journal* on the Closing Date (or, if the Closing Date is not a Business Day, on the immediately preceding Business Day), calculated on the basis of a 365-day year and the actual number of days elapsed.
**Section 2.05 Earnout**

**(a)** *Maximum Earnout Payment.* If the Company\'s Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period (the twelve (12) month period ending December 31, 2026) equals or exceeds Thirty-Eight Million Dollars (\$38,000,000), Buyer shall pay to Seller an amount equal to Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) (the \"Maximum Earnout Payment\").

**(b)** *Pro-Rata Earnout.* If the Company\'s Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period is at least Thirty-Two Million Dollars (\$32,000,000) but less than Thirty-Eight Million Dollars (\$38,000,000), Buyer shall pay to Seller an amount (the \"Earnout Payment\") equal to: (\$25,000,000 ÷ (\$38,000,000 -- \$32,000,000)) × (Actual Adjusted EBITDA -- \$32,000,000). For the avoidance of doubt, this formula results in a linear interpolation, such that the Earnout Payment increases by approximately Four Million One Hundred Sixty-Six Thousand Six Hundred Sixty-Seven Dollars (\$4,166,667) for each One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000) of Adjusted EBITDA in excess of \$32,000,000. If the Company\'s Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period is less than \$32,000,000, no Earnout Payment shall be due or payable.

**(c)** *Earnout Calculation and Dispute Resolution.* Within sixty (60) days after the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall prepare and deliver to Seller a written statement (the \"Earnout Statement\") setting forth Buyer\'s good-faith calculation of Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period, together with reasonable supporting documentation. Seller shall have thirty (30) days to review the Earnout Statement and deliver any objections thereto. The dispute resolution procedures set forth in Section 2.04(b) and Section 2.04(c) shall apply *mutatis mutandis* to any dispute with respect to the Earnout Statement.

**(d)** *Operation of the Business During the Earnout Period.* From and after the Closing Date through the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall, and shall cause the Company to, operate the business of the Company in a manner consistent with past practice and in good faith to maximize the Earnout Payment. Without limiting the foregoing, Buyer shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, take any action that would reasonably be expected to reduce the Adjusted EBITDA of the Company below the levels that would otherwise have been achieved. In furtherance of the foregoing, during the Earnout Period, Buyer shall cause the Company to maintain substantially the same level of personnel, equipment, and other resources as in effect immediately prior to the Closing Date and shall not divert or redirect any contracts, customers, revenues, or business opportunities of the Company to Buyer or any of its Affiliates. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Buyer acknowledges and agrees that Seller shall have no obligation to contribute resources, personnel, or funds to the Company during the Earnout Period, and the obligations set forth in this Section 2.05(d) are solely obligations of Buyer.

**(e)** *Payment of Earnout.* Any Earnout Payment determined to be payable pursuant to this Section 2.05 shall be paid by Buyer to Seller within ten (10) Business Days after the final determination of Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period (whether by agreement of the Parties, expiration of the review period without objection, or determination of the Independent Accountant), by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Seller. For U.S. federal income tax purposes, the Parties agree to treat any Earnout Payment as an adjustment to the Purchase Price.

> \(vii\) evidence reasonably satisfactory to Buyer that all contracts, agreements, and arrangements between the Company and Seller or any Affiliate of Seller (other than the affiliate lease described on Schedule 4.09, which shall be addressed separately by the Parties) have been terminated effective as of or prior to the Closing without any remaining liability of the Company;

> \(viii\) a certificate of an authorized officer of Seller, dated as of the Closing Date, certifying that the conditions set forth in Section 7.02(a), Section 7.02(b), and Section 7.02(c) have been satisfied; and

> \(ix\) a certificate of the secretary or an assistant secretary of Seller, dated as of the Closing Date, certifying as to (A) the certificate of incorporation and bylaws of Seller, (B) the articles of incorporation and bylaws of the Company, and (C) the incumbency and specimen signatures of the officers of Seller executing this Agreement and the Transaction Documents.
**(b)** *Buyer Deliverables.* At the Closing, Buyer shall deliver, or cause to be delivered, to Seller the following:
> \(i\) the Closing Payment, by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account or accounts designated in writing by Seller in accordance with Section 2.03(b);
> \(ii\) the Escrow Amount, by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the Escrow Agent in accordance with Section 2.03(c) and the Escrow Agreement;

> \(iii\) certified copies of the resolutions duly adopted by the members or managers of Buyer (as applicable) authorizing the execution, delivery, and performance by Buyer of this Agreement and the Transaction Documents and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby;
> \(iv\) the Escrow Agreement, duly executed by Buyer;

> \(v\) a certificate of an authorized officer or manager of Buyer, dated as of the Closing Date, certifying that the conditions set forth in Section 7.03(a) and Section 7.03(b) have been satisfied; and
> \(vi\) evidence of Buyer\'s organizational good standing issued by the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware, dated not more than ten (10) days prior to the Closing Date.
**[ARTICLE III]{.underline}**
**[REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF SELLER]{.underline}**
Seller represents and warrants to Buyer as follows:
**Section 3.01 Organization and Good Standing**

Seller is a corporation duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware. Seller has full corporate power and authority to own, lease, and operate its properties and assets and to carry on its business as presently conducted. Seller is duly qualified or licensed to do business and is in good standing in each jurisdiction where the nature of its business or the ownership or leasing of its properties requires such qualification.
**Section 3.02 Authority; Binding Effect**

Seller has full corporate power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform its obligations under this Agreement and each other Transaction Document to which it is or will be a party, and to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby. The execution, delivery, and performance by Seller of this Agreement and each other Transaction Document to which it is or will be a party, and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby, have been duly and validly authorized by all necessary corporate action on the part of Seller, including approval by Seller\'s board of directors. No other corporate proceedings on the part of Seller are necessary to authorize the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement or to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby. This Agreement has been, and at the Closing each other Transaction Document to which Seller is or will be a party will be, duly and validly executed and delivered by Seller and, assuming the due authorization, execution, and delivery by the other parties hereto and thereto, constitutes, or upon execution and delivery will constitute, a legal, valid, and binding obligation of Seller, enforceable against Seller in accordance with its terms, subject to (a) applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, fraudulent conveyance, and similar Laws affecting creditors\' rights and remedies generally and (b) general principles of equity (whether applied in a proceeding at law or in equity).
**Section 3.03 Ownership of Shares**

Seller is the record and beneficial owner of 1,000,000 shares of common stock, par value \$0.01 per share, of the Company, which constitute all of the issued and outstanding shares of capital stock of the Company, free and clear of all Encumbrances (other than restrictions arising under applicable securities Laws). There are no outstanding options, warrants, convertible securities, rights of first refusal, rights of first offer, preemptive rights, subscription rights, or other rights, agreements, commitments, or arrangements of any kind relating to the Shares or obligating Seller to transfer or dispose of any Shares. Upon delivery of the Shares to Buyer at the Closing in accordance with this Agreement, Buyer will acquire good and valid title to the Shares, free and clear of all Encumbrances (other than restrictions arising under applicable securities Laws and Encumbrances created by or through Buyer).
**Section 3.04 No Conflicts; Consents**

The execution, delivery, and performance by Seller of this Agreement and the other Transaction Documents, and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby, do not and will not (a) conflict with or violate the certificate of incorporation or bylaws (or other organizational documents) of Seller, (b) conflict with or violate any Law or order applicable to Seller or by which any property or asset of Seller is bound or affected, (c) result in any breach of or constitute a default (or an event that, with the giving of notice or lapse of time, or both, would become a default) under, give rise to a right of termination, cancellation, modification, or acceleration of any obligation under, or result in the creation of any Encumbrance upon any of the properties or assets of Seller under, any contract, agreement, instrument, Permit, or other arrangement to which Seller is a party or by which Seller or any of its properties or assets is bound or affected, or (d) require any filing with, notification to, consent, approval, authorization, or waiver of, or any order, registration, or declaration from, any Governmental Authority or other Person, except (with respect to clause (d)) (i) filings required under the HSR Act and (ii) as set forth on Schedule 3.04.
**Section 3.05 Litigation**

There are no Actions pending or, to the Knowledge of the Company, threatened against Seller that would reasonably be expected to adversely affect or restrict Seller\'s ability to execute, deliver, and perform this Agreement and the other Transaction Documents or to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby.
**Section 3.06 Brokers**

Neither Seller nor any of its Affiliates has retained or authorized any broker, finder, financial advisor, investment banker, or other intermediary who might be entitled to any fee or commission in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, except as set forth on Schedule 3.06.
**[ARTICLE IV]{.underline}**
**[REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES REGARDING THE COMPANY]{.underline}**

Seller represents and warrants to Buyer that, except as set forth in the Disclosure Schedules delivered by Seller to Buyer concurrently with the execution and delivery of this Agreement (the \"Disclosure Schedules\"), the following representations and warranties are true and correct as of the date hereof:
**Section 4.01 Organization and Qualification**

The Company is a corporation duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of Oregon. The Company has full corporate power and authority to own, lease, and operate its properties and assets and to carry on its business as currently conducted. The Company is duly qualified or licensed to do business and is in good standing in each jurisdiction where the character of its properties owned or leased or the nature of its business makes such qualification or licensing necessary, including the States of Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada. Seller has made available to Buyer true, correct, and complete copies of the articles of incorporation and bylaws of the Company, as currently in effect.
**Section 4.02 Authority**

The Company has full corporate power and authority to execute and deliver this Agreement to the extent it is a party hereto and to perform its obligations hereunder. The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement by the Company (to the extent it is a party hereto) have been duly and validly authorized by all necessary corporate action on the part of the Company.
**Section 4.03 Capitalization**

The authorized capital stock of the Company consists of 5,000,000 shares of common stock, par value \$0.01 per share, of which 1,000,000 shares are issued and outstanding as of the date hereof. All of the issued and outstanding shares of common stock of the Company have been duly authorized, are validly issued, fully paid, and nonassessable, and were issued in compliance with all applicable Laws and in accordance with the Company\'s articles of incorporation and bylaws. There are no outstanding options, warrants, convertible or exchangeable securities, subscriptions, rights (including preemptive rights or rights of first refusal), stock appreciation rights, phantom stock, profit participation, calls, commitments, or agreements of any kind relating to the capital stock of the Company, or obligating the Company to issue, deliver, sell, repurchase, or redeem any shares of its capital stock. There are no outstanding or authorized equity-based awards, stock appreciation rights, phantom stock awards, profit interests, or similar rights with respect to the Company. There are no outstanding agreements, contracts, or commitments restricting the transfer of, or requiring the registration for sale of, any shares of the capital stock of the Company. There are no anti-dilution or similar adjustments with respect to any equity securities of the Company.
**Section 4.04 Subsidiaries**

The Company does not own, directly or indirectly, any equity interest, capital stock, membership interest, partnership interest, joint venture interest, or other ownership interest in any other Person. The Company has no subsidiaries.
**Section 4.05 No Conflicts; Consents**

611: **(c)** *Remedies.* The Parties acknowledge and agree that a breach of any of the restrictive covenants set forth in this Section 6.09 would cause irreparable damage to Buyer and the Company and that monetary damages alone would not provide an adequate remedy. The execution, delivery, and performance by the Company of this Agreement (to the extent it is a party hereto), and the consummation of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, do not and will not (a) conflict with or violate the articles of incorporation or bylaws (or other organizational documents) of the Company, (b) conflict with or violate any Law or order applicable to the Company or by which any property or asset of the Company is bound or affected, or (c) result in any breach of or constitute a default (or an event that, with the giving of notice or lapse of time, or both, would become a default) under, give rise to a right of termination, cancellation, modification, or acceleration of, or result in the creation of any Encumbrance upon any of the properties or assets of the Company under, any contract, agreement, instrument, Permit, or other arrangement to which the Company is a party or by which the Company or any of its properties or assets is bound or affected, except, in each case of clauses (b) and (c), where such conflict, violation, breach, or default would not, individually or in the aggregate, be material to the Company. Seller has delivered to Buyer (a) the audited balance sheets of the Company as of December 31, 2022, December 31, 2023, and December 31, 2024, and the related audited statements of income, stockholders\' equity, and cash flows for each of the fiscal years then ended, together with the reports thereon of Winslow & Tate CPA Group, independent certified public accountants, and (b) the unaudited balance sheet of the Company as of September 30, 2025, and the related unaudited statements of income and cash flows for the nine-month period then ended (the financial statements described in clauses (a) and (b) above, collectively, the \"Financial Statements\"). The Company does not have any liabilities, obligations, or commitments of a type that would be required to be reflected on a balance sheet prepared in accordance with GAAP, except (a) liabilities reflected or reserved against in the Financial Statements, (b) liabilities incurred since September 30, 2025 in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice (none of which results from, arises out of, relates to, or was caused by any breach of contract, breach of warranty, tort, infringement, or violation of Law), (c) liabilities arising under the executory portions of contracts to which the Company is a party (not resulting from any breach or default by the Company), (d) Transaction Expenses, and (e) liabilities set forth on Schedule 4.07.

**(a)** For a period of not less than twelve (12) months following the Closing Date, Buyer shall, or shall cause the Company to, provide each employee of the Company who continues in employment with the Company following the Closing (each, a \"Continuing Employee\") with (i) base salary or wages at least equal to the base salary or wages provided to such Continuing Employee immediately prior to the Closing, and (ii) employee benefits that are, in the aggregate, substantially comparable to those provided to such Continuing Employee immediately prior to the Closing. Nothing in this Section 6.08 shall be construed to guarantee employment for any specific period of time, to restrict Buyer\'s or the Company\'s right to terminate the employment of any employee, or to create any third-party beneficiary rights in favor of any employee.

**(b)** With respect to any Employee Benefit Plan maintained by Buyer or the Company following the Closing, Buyer shall, or shall cause the Company to, credit each Continuing Employee with his or her years of service with the Company (and any predecessor entities) prior to the Closing Date for purposes of eligibility to participate, vesting, and benefit accrual (but not for purposes of benefit accrual under any defined benefit pension plan).

**(c)** Buyer shall, or shall cause the Company to, permit each Continuing Employee who participates in the Company\'s 401(k) plan to roll over his or her account balance under such plan into a tax-qualified defined contribution plan maintained by Buyer or the Company following the Closing, in accordance with applicable Law.
**Section 6.09 Non-Competition; Non-Solicitation**

**(a)** *Non-Competition.* For a period of five (5) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, engage in, own, manage, operate, control, participate in, consult with, render services for, or in any manner be connected with any business anywhere in the United States; *provided* that the foregoing shall not restrict Seller or its Affiliates from (i) owning, directly or indirectly, solely as a passive investment, securities of any Person that are traded on a national securities exchange if Seller and its Affiliates do not, directly or indirectly, beneficially own five percent (5%) or more of any class of securities of such Person, or (ii) performing its obligations under this Agreement and the other Transaction Documents.

**(b)** *Non-Solicitation.* For a period of three (3) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, (i) solicit, recruit, hire, or engage (or attempt to solicit, recruit, hire, or engage) any employee of the Company, or (ii) solicit or encourage (or attempt to solicit or encourage) any customer, supplier, licensee, licensor, or other business relationship of the Company to cease or reduce its business with the Company; *provided* that the foregoing shall not restrict (A) general solicitations of employment not specifically directed toward employees of the Company, including through advertisements in newspapers, trade journals, or online job boards, or (B) solicitations by headhunters or recruiting firms not specifically directed by Seller or its Affiliates to target employees of the Company.

**(c)** *Remedies.* The Parties acknowledge and agree that a breach of any of the restrictive covenants set forth in this Section 6.09 would cause irreparable damage to Buyer and the Company and that monetary damages alone would not provide an adequate remedy. Accordingly, in the event of any actual or threatened breach by Seller or any of its Affiliates of the provisions of this Section 6.09, Buyer and the Company shall be entitled to seek specific performance and injunctive relief (temporary, preliminary, and permanent) from any court of competent jurisdiction, without the necessity of proving actual damages or posting any bond, in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity. The restrictive covenants contained in this Section 6.09 are independent of any other provision of this Agreement, and the existence of any claim or cause of action of Seller against Buyer, whether predicated on this Agreement or otherwise, shall not constitute a defense to the enforcement of such restrictive covenants.
**Section 6.10 Directors\' and Officers\' Insurance**

For a period of six (6) years following the Closing Date, Buyer shall cause the Company to maintain in effect directors\' and officers\' liability insurance (\"D&O Tail Insurance\") covering acts or omissions occurring at or prior to the Closing Date with respect to those Persons who are or were directors or officers of the Company at or prior to the Closing Date, on terms (including coverage amounts, retentions, and other material terms) that are no less favorable in the aggregate than the D&O insurance maintained by the Company as of the date of this Agreement; *provided* that the annual premium for such D&O Tail Insurance shall not exceed 250% of the annual premium currently paid by the Company for its existing D&O insurance.
**Section 6.11 Further Assurances**

From time to time following the Closing, each Party shall, and shall cause its Affiliates to, execute and deliver such additional documents, instruments, conveyances, and assurances, and take such further actions as may be reasonably required to carry out the provisions of this Agreement and the other Transaction Documents and to give effect to the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby.
**[ARTICLE VII]{.underline}**
**[CONDITIONS TO CLOSING]{.underline}**
**Section 7.01 Conditions to Each Party\'s Obligations**

The respective obligations of each Party to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall be subject to the satisfaction (or, to the extent permitted by applicable Law, waiver by each Party) at or prior to the Closing of the following conditions:

**(a)** No Governmental Authority shall have enacted, issued, promulgated, enforced, or entered any Law, order, injunction, judgment, decree, ruling, or other legally binding action (whether temporary, preliminary, or permanent) that is then in effect and that has the effect of making the transactions contemplated by this Agreement illegal or otherwise preventing or prohibiting the consummation of such transactions.
**(b)** The applicable waiting period (and any extension thereof) under the HSR Act in respect of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall have expired or been terminated.

Accordingly, each Party shall be entitled to an injunction or injunctions, specific performance, and other equitable remedies to prevent breaches of this Agreement and to enforce specifically the terms and provisions hereof, in addition to any other remedy to which such Party may be entitled at law or in equity. Each Party further agrees that (a) it will not oppose the granting of specific performance and other equitable remedies on the basis that the other Party has an adequate remedy at law or that an award of specific performance is not an appropriate remedy for any reason at law or in equity, and (b) no Party shall be required to provide or post any bond or other security or collateral in connection with any such order or injunction.

lines.text: **Section 10.05 Entire Agreement**

This Agreement, together with the Disclosure Schedules, Exhibits, and the other Transaction Documents, constitutes the entire agreement among the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous agreements, understandings, negotiations, and discussions, whether written or oral, of the Parties relating thereto, including the letter of intent dated August 15, 2025 and the term sheet dated September 10, 2025 between Seller and Buyer.
**Section 10.06 Amendments and Waivers**

No amendment, modification, or supplement to this Agreement shall be effective unless it is in writing and signed by Buyer and Seller. No waiver of any provision of this Agreement shall be effective unless it is in writing and signed by the Party or Parties against whom enforcement of the waiver is sought. No waiver by any Party of any breach or violation of, default under, or inaccuracy in any representation, warranty, covenant, or agreement contained in this Agreement, whether intentional or not, shall be deemed to extend to any prior or subsequent breach, violation, default, or inaccuracy, or affect in any way any rights arising by virtue of any prior or subsequent such occurrence.
**Section 10.07 Severability**

If any term or provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable under applicable Law in any jurisdiction, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect any other term or provision of this Agreement or invalidate or render unenforceable such term or provision in any other jurisdiction. Upon a determination that any term or provision is invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith to modify this Agreement to give effect, to the greatest extent possible, to the original intent of the Parties, and the remaining provisions of this Agreement shall continue in full force and effect.
**Section 10.08 Successors and Assigns**

This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the Parties and their respective successors and permitted assigns. Neither Party may assign this Agreement or any of its rights, interests, or obligations hereunder without the prior written consent of the other Party; *provided* that Buyer may, without the consent of Seller, (a) assign any or all of its rights, interests, or obligations under this Agreement to one or more of its Affiliates, and (b) collaterally assign its rights (but not its obligations) under this Agreement to Clearwater Environmental Lending Corp. or any other lender providing financing in connection with the transactions contemplated hereby, as collateral security; *provided*, *further*, that no such assignment shall relieve Buyer of any of its obligations under this Agreement.
**Section 10.09 Third-Party Beneficiaries**

This Agreement is for the sole benefit of the Parties and their respective successors and permitted assigns, and nothing herein, express or implied, is intended to or shall confer upon any other Person any legal or equitable right, benefit, or remedy of any nature whatsoever under or by reason of this Agreement; *provided* that the Buyer Indemnitees and the Seller Indemnitees shall be intended third-party beneficiaries of, and shall be entitled to enforce, the applicable provisions of Article IX.
**Section 10.10 Specific Performance**

The Parties acknowledge and agree that irreparable damage would occur and that the Parties would not have any adequate remedy at law in the event that any of the provisions of this Agreement were not performed in accordance with their specific terms or were otherwise breached. Accordingly, each Party shall be entitled to an injunction or injunctions, specific performance, and other equitable remedies to prevent breaches of this Agreement and to enforce specifically the terms and provisions hereof, in addition to any other remedy to which such Party may be entitled at law or in equity. Each Party further agrees that (a) it will not oppose the granting of specific performance and other equitable remedies on the basis that the other Party has an adequate remedy at law or that an award of specific performance is not an appropriate remedy for any reason at law or in equity, and (b) no Party shall be required to provide or post any bond or other security or collateral in connection with any such order or injunction.
**Section 10.11 Counterparts; Electronic Signatures**

This Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, but all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart of a signature page to this Agreement by email (including any electronic signature complying with the U.S. ESIGN Act of 2000, the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act, or any similar Law) shall be effective as delivery of a manually executed counterpart to this Agreement.
**Section 10.12 Expenses**

Except as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement, the provisions regarding the allocation of costs, fees, and expenses set forth in Section 8.03 shall apply with respect to the transactions contemplated hereby.

321: The Special Indemnity is a distinct indemnification mechanism that operates separately from and in addition to the general representation and warranty indemnification. Its parameters are as follows:
322: 
323: **Survival.** The Special Indemnity must survive for seventy-two (72) months (six years) post-closing. This extended survival period reflects the long-tail nature of CERCLA and environmental enforcement actions, which --- as discussed in Section 4.2 --- often take years to progress from initial inquiry to resolution. A seventy-two month survival period provides the buyer with a meaningful window within which to assert claims as the environmental matter develops and the buyer\'s actual losses become ascertainable.
324: 
325: **Not Subject to the Basket/Deductible.** The Special Indemnity is a dollar-one indemnification obligation. It is not subject to the general deductible described in Section 5.2. The rationale is straightforward: the basket/deductible is designed to filter out immaterial or de minimis claims arising from general representation breaches. A known environmental liability with an estimated exposure of \$1,000,000 or more is, by definition, not immaterial --- it is a specifically identified risk that has been factored into the purchase price negotiation and that requires dedicated indemnification protection.
326: 
327: **Not Subject to the General Cap.** The Special Indemnity is not counted toward the general indemnification cap described in Section 5.1. It operates as a separate, independent indemnification obligation with its own limitations. The Special Indemnity may be subject to its own sub-cap, which is negotiated on a matter-specific basis and typically reflects the high end of the estimated liability range identified in the environmental due diligence. For example, if the estimated liability range for a CERCLA exposure is \$1,500,000 to \$6,000,000, the Special Indemnity sub-cap might be negotiated at \$6,000,000 or \$7,500,000 (the high end of the range plus a reasonable buffer).
328: 
329: **Escrow.** Escrow funds designated for the Special Indemnity should be held for thirty-six (36) months post-closing, consistent with the extended escrow for Fundamental Representations described in Section 5.4. After thirty-six months, the buyer may still assert Special Indemnity claims (through the seventy-two month survival period), but recovery would be sought directly from the seller rather than from escrow.
330: 
331: **Specific Identification.** The Special Indemnity provision must specifically identify the environmental matter by name, site location, applicable regulatory proceeding number (if any), nature of the liability (e.g., \"CERCLA response cost liability arising from historical disposal at \[Site Name\]\"), and the specific representation or due diligence finding that identified the matter. The identified matters should be listed on a dedicated schedule to the SPA (typically a \"Schedule of Scheduled Environmental Matters\" or similar title).
332: 
333: **Rationale.** Known environmental liabilities are not appropriately covered by general representation and warranty indemnification for several reasons:
334: 
335: > \(i\) Known environmental matters are already disclosed (and, in many cases, scheduled as exceptions to the environmental representations). Because they are disclosed, they may not technically constitute \"breaches\" of the representations in the traditional sense, potentially leaving the buyer without a general indemnification claim.
336: >
337: > \(ii\) General survival periods (whether eighteen months for general representations or even thirty-six months for environmental representations) are inadequate for the long-tail nature of many environmental enforcement actions, which may take five to ten years to resolve.
338: >
339: > \(iii\) The basket/deductible could prevent recovery for environmental matters falling within the lower end of the estimated liability range, particularly where the buyer has other general indemnification claims consuming the deductible.
340: >
341: > \(iv\) The general indemnification cap may be consumed by other claims, leaving the buyer unprotected for the specific known liability that was the subject of purchase price negotiation.
342: 
343: **Specific Instruction.** If environmental due diligence has identified a known CERCLA exposure --- such as a pending EPA information request at a specific disposal facility --- with an estimated liability range of \$1,500,000 to \$6,000,000, the associate MUST ensure that the SPA contains a Special Indemnity provision specifically covering that exposure. If the seller\'s draft SPA fails to include such a provision, the associate should draft and insert a Special Indemnity provision and raise it with the seller\'s counsel as a required addition. Do not treat the absence of a Special Indemnity as a minor markup item; it is a **Critical** priority item that must be escalated to the responsible partner if the seller resists.
344: 
345: **Sample Special Indemnity Language:**
346: 
347: > *\"(a) From and after the Closing, Seller shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Buyer and its Affiliates (including, after the Closing, the Company) and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns (collectively, the \'Buyer Indemnified Parties\') from and against any and all Losses arising out of, resulting from, or relating to the Scheduled Environmental Matters set forth on Schedule 6.1 (the \'Special Environmental Indemnity\').*
348: >
349: > *\"(b) The Special Environmental Indemnity shall survive the Closing for a period of seventy-two (72) months following the Closing Date, and any claim for indemnification under this Section \[\_\_\] must be asserted by written notice delivered to Seller on or prior to the date that is seventy-two (72) months following the Closing Date.*
350: >
351: > *\"(c) The Special Environmental Indemnity shall not be subject to the Deductible set forth in Section \[\_\_\] or the Cap set forth in Section \[\_\_\]. The maximum aggregate liability of Seller under this Section \[\_\_\] with respect to each Scheduled Environmental Matter shall be the amount set forth opposite such Scheduled Environmental Matter on Schedule 6.1 (each, a \'Special Indemnity Sub-Cap\').*
352: >
353: > *\"(d) For the avoidance of doubt, Losses recovered by Buyer Indemnified Parties pursuant to this Section \[\_\_\] shall not reduce or otherwise affect the Cap available for claims under Section \[\_\_\].\"*
