add_issue(13, 'Sections 9.02 and 9.04', 'Dalton Creek Special Indemnity', 'HIGH',
    'Executed Term Sheet §9; Environmental DD §§III.A–C; Playbook §6; partner instructions ¶¶168–180',
    '''Section 9.02 contains general indemnification for breaches, covenants, Transaction Expenses, and Pre-Closing Taxes, but no Special Indemnity for Dalton Creek.

Section 9.04(a) applies the Basket to Section 9.02(a) claims other than Fundamental Representations. Section 9.04(b) applies the Indemnification Cap to non-Fundamental Representation claims. Section 9.08 provides a 36-month hold only for amounts retained as a Pending Claims Reserve relating to Fundamental Representations.''',
    '''Add the following as new Section 9.02(e):

(e) Dalton Creek Special Indemnity. From and after the Closing, Seller shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Buyer Indemnitees from and against any and all Losses arising out of, resulting from, or relating to (i) the pending information request issued by the United States Environmental Protection Agency under Section 104(e) of CERCLA concerning the Company’s former operations at the Dalton Creek disposal facility located in Clackamas County, Oregon, (ii) any investigation, notice, claim, demand, enforcement action, order, consent decree, administrative proceeding, contribution claim, cost-recovery action, or other proceeding by any Governmental Authority or third party relating to the Dalton Creek facility or such information request, and (iii) any contamination, response costs, remediation obligations, natural-resource damages, defense costs, settlement costs, penalties, fines, or other liabilities arising from or relating to the Company’s former operations, waste handling, treatment, transportation, or disposal activities at the Dalton Creek facility (the “Dalton Creek Special Indemnity”).

The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall not be subject to the Basket Amount or the Indemnification Cap, and Losses indemnifiable under this Section 9.02(e) shall not be counted toward, or reduce, the Basket Amount, the Indemnification Cap, or any other limitation applicable to claims under Section 9.02(a). Add the following to Section 9.04(a):

The Basket Amount shall not apply to Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations, Fraud or willful misconduct, or the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity.

Add the following to Section 9.04(d):

The Escrow Fund shall include a portion designated for claims under the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, which portion shall remain available for such claims until the date that is thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date, subject to the terms of the Escrow Agreement. The release of such portion after that date shall not limit the Buyer Indemnitees’ right to pursue the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity directly against Seller through the 72-month survival period.''',
    'The DD memo estimates Dalton Creek exposure at $1.5 million–$6 million and identifies the EPA CERCLA §104(e) request as a precursor to possible PRP designation, investigation, cleanup, and enforcement. The term sheet expressly requires a Special Indemnity with 72-month survival, outside the general basket and cap, supported by escrow for 36 months. The draft’s omission is a direct departure from an agreed economic term and could leave a disclosed matter outside the breach-based indemnity framework.',
    'Confirm the dedicated escrow allocation with the client. The term sheet requires that a portion of the $16.125 million escrow be available for Dalton Creek claims and held for 36 months, but does not state the exact allocation. The playbook suggests sizing dedicated support at least to the low end of the estimate ($1.5 million); separate escrow is preferable if administratively feasible.'

add_issue(1, 'Section 1.01', 'Material Adverse Effect definition', 'CRITICAL',
    'Executed Term Sheet §12(c); Playbook §§2.1–2.2 and 14; Environmental DD §§III–VI; partner instructions ¶¶52–67',
    '''“Material Adverse Effect” means any event, change, effect, development, state of facts, condition, circumstance, or occurrence that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or results of operations of the Company, or (b) the ability of Seller to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement; provided, however, that none of the following, individually or in the aggregate, shall be deemed to constitute, or shall be taken into account in determining whether there has been or would reasonably be expected to be, a Material Adverse Effect: (i) changes in general economic, financial, credit, securities market, or political conditions in the United States or globally; (ii) changes in conditions generally affecting the environmental services industry; (iii) changes in Environmental Laws or regulations; (iv) changes in GAAP or applicable Law (other than Environmental Laws, which are addressed in clause (iii) above); (v) acts of war … epidemics, pandemics, earthquakes, hurricanes, tornados, floods, or other natural disasters or acts of God; (vi) the announcement or pendency of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement …; (vii) any action taken by the Company at the express written request or with the express written consent of Buyer; and (viii) any failure by the Company to meet any internal or external projections …''',
    '''“Material Adverse Effect” means any event, change, effect, development, state of facts, condition, circumstance, or occurrence that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or results of operations of the Company, or (b) the ability of Seller to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement; provided, however, that none of the following, individually or in the aggregate, shall be deemed to constitute, or shall be taken into account in determining whether there has been or would reasonably be expected to be, a Material Adverse Effect: (i) changes in general economic, financial, credit, securities market, or political conditions in the United States or globally; (ii) changes in conditions generally affecting the environmental services industry; (iii) changes in Environmental Laws or regulations; (iv) changes in GAAP or applicable Law (other than Environmental Laws, which are addressed in clause (iii) above); (v) acts of war (whether or not declared), armed hostilities, sabotage, terrorism, military actions, or any escalation or worsening thereof, epidemics, pandemics, earthquakes, hurricanes, tornados, floods, or other natural disasters or acts of God; (vi) the announcement or pendency of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, including any impact on relationships with customers, suppliers, employees, or Governmental Authorities; (vii) any action taken by the Company at the express written request or with the express written consent of Buyer; and (viii) any failure by the Company to meet any internal or external projections, forecasts, or estimates of revenue, earnings, or other financial performance metrics for any period; provided, further, that, with respect to clauses (i) through (vi), such change, effect, event, or development shall be taken into account in determining whether a Material Adverse Effect has occurred or would reasonably be expected to occur to the extent such change, effect, event, or development disproportionately affects the Company and its Subsidiaries, taken as a whole, relative to other participants in the industries in which the Company and its Subsidiaries operate.''',
    'The draft’s industry-specific and Environmental Law carve-outs omit the required disproportionate-impact exception. Cascadia’s value is concentrated in environmental remediation, hazardous waste management, permits, and government contracts; therefore, an industry-wide or regulatory development can materially affect this target even if it is characterized as general. The revised language preserves customary carve-outs but prevents those carve-outs from insulating target-specific or disproportionate harm, including a regulatory development affecting Cascadia’s disposal, remediation, or permit profile. This is the playbook’s stated non-negotiable position and is particularly important given the Dalton Creek and permit risks identified in diligence.',
    'Conform “Company and its Subsidiaries” to the SPA’s defined terms; if the Company has no subsidiaries, “Company, taken as a whole” is acceptable. Do not add a litigation carve-out; the playbook cautions against excluding environmental claims from the MAE analysis.'
)

add_issue(2, 'Section 1.01', 'Indemnification Cap definition', 'HIGH',

The playbook instructs that the executed term sheet controls economic terms and that a deviation must be corrected without treating it as a drafting gray area.',
    'The cap is for Losses arising from breaches of non-Fundamental Representations. Fundamental Representation liability remains subject to the Purchase Price cap, and the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity must remain outside the general cap.'
)

add_heading('Article II — Purchase and Sale; Purchase Price', level=2)
add_issue(3, 'Section 2.05', 'Earnout covenant and financial mechanics', 'CRITICAL',
    'Executed Term Sheet §5; Playbook §§7.1–7.2; partner instructions ¶¶88–111',
    '''(c) Within sixty (60) days after the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall prepare and deliver to Seller a written statement … setting forth Buyer’s good-faith calculation of Adjusted EBITDA …

(d) From and after the Closing Date through the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall, and shall cause the Company to, operate the business of the Company in a manner consistent with past practice and in good faith to maximize the Earnout Payment. … Buyer shall cause the Company to maintain substantially the same level of personnel, equipment, and other resources … and shall not divert or redirect any contracts, customers, revenues, or business opportunities …

(e) Any Earnout Payment … shall be paid … within ten (10) Business Days after the final determination of Adjusted EBITDA …''',
    '''Replace Section 2.05(c), (d), and (e) in their entirety with the following:

(c) Within forty-five (45) days following the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall prepare and deliver to Seller a written statement (the “Earnout Statement”) setting forth Buyer’s good-faith calculation of Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period and the resulting Earnout Payment, if any, together with reasonable supporting detail. Seller shall have thirty (30) days following receipt of the Earnout Statement to review the Earnout Statement and deliver a written notice of objection specifying in reasonable detail each disputed item and the amount Seller believes to be correct. Any dispute not resolved by the Parties within twenty (20) Business Days after delivery of such notice shall be submitted to the Independent Accountant under Section 2.04(c), whose determination shall be final and binding absent manifest error.

(d) Following the Closing, Buyer shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, take any action with the primary purpose of avoiding or reducing the Earnout Payment. For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this Section 2.05(d) shall restrict Buyer’s right to operate, integrate, restructure, or otherwise manage the Company and its business in Buyer’s sole discretion, including the right to make capital expenditure decisions, change pricing or compensation, make strategic investments, acquire or dispose of businesses or assets, reorganize the Company or its operations, allocate resources, or take any other operational action, and no such action shall constitute a breach of this Section 2.05(d) unless taken with the primary purpose of avoiding or reducing the Earnout Payment. Buyer shall have no affirmative obligation to operate the Company in any particular manner, to maximize the Earnout Payment, to maintain the Company as a separate entity, to maintain any particular level of personnel, equipment, capital expenditures, or resources, to retain any employee, or to refrain from diverting or redirecting contracts, customers, revenues, or business opportunities, in each case except to the extent an action is taken with the primary purpose of avoiding or reducing the Earnout Payment.

(e) Any Earnout Payment determined to be payable pursuant to this Section 2.05 shall be paid by Buyer to Seller within sixty (60) days following the end of the Earnout Period, subject to final determination under this Section 2.05, by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Seller. For U.S. federal income tax purposes, the Parties agree to treat any Earnout Payment as an adjustment to the Purchase Price.''',
    'The seller’s affirmative operating obligations would effectively give Seller veto rights over Buyer’s platform integration, restructuring, personnel, capital allocation, and bolt-on strategy through December 31, 2026. The playbook permits only a narrow negative covenant against actions taken with the primary purpose of avoiding or reducing the earnout. The economic thresholds in the draft are correct ($25 million maximum; $38 million full-payment threshold; $32 million floor; linear interpolation), but the timing is not: the term sheet requires the calculation within 45 days and payment within 60 days after the Measurement Period. The replacement language preserves the agreed economics and restores Buyer’s operational flexibility.',
    'Confirm that the final Exhibit D includes the agreed Adjusted EBITDA methodology and add-backs for buyer-directed integration costs, restructuring charges, non-recurring items, and post-closing affiliate/corporate allocations not charged consistently before Closing.'
)

add_issue(4, 'Sections 2.03(d), 2.08(a), and 7.02', 'Debt payoff letters, funds flow, and closing condition', 'HIGH',
    'Executed Term Sheet §6; Playbook §9.2; partner instructions ¶¶193–205; Clearwater Environmental Lending Corp. financing context',
    '''Section 2.03(d): “At or promptly following the Closing, Buyer shall cause the Company to repay, discharge, and satisfy in full all Closing Indebtedness. Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cooperate with Buyer in connection with the repayment of such Closing Indebtedness.”

Section 2.08(a): Seller’s closing deliverables do not include payoff letters.

Section 7.02: Buyer’s conditions do not include delivery of payoff letters.''',
    '''Replace Section 2.03(d) with:

(d) At the Closing, all Closing Indebtedness shall be repaid, discharged, and satisfied in full through the closing funds flow. Seller shall deliver to Buyer executed payoff letters from each holder of Closing Indebtedness no later than three (3) Business Days prior to the Closing Date, including Cascade Mutual Bank in respect of the $28,000,000 senior term loan, Pacific Lease Corp. in respect of the $9,800,000 equipment financing, and Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc. in respect of the $4,500,000 subordinated seller note. Each payoff letter shall state the total amount required to repay the applicable indebtedness in full as of the Closing Date, including principal, accrued and unpaid interest, prepayment premiums, breakage costs, and all other amounts necessary to satisfy the obligation; provide wire transfer instructions; and provide for the prompt release of all liens, security interests, mortgages, pledges, and other Encumbrances securing such indebtedness, including delivery of UCC-3 termination statements and other lien-release instruments.

Add Section 2.03(e):

(e) The Parties shall execute a funds flow agreement at least two (2) Business Days prior to the Closing Date setting forth the amounts and wire instructions for all Closing payments, including repayment of all Closing Indebtedness, payment of Seller Transaction Expenses, deposit of the Escrow Amount with Pinnacle Trust Company, and payment of the balance of the Purchase Price to Seller.

Add Section 2.08(a)(x):

(x) the executed payoff letters required by Section 2.03(d), together with all payoff statements and lien-release documentation required to implement the Closing funds flow.

Add Section 7.02(h):

(h) Seller shall have delivered the payoff letters required by Section 2.03(d), and the funds flow agreement required by Section 2.03(e) shall have been executed by the Parties.''',
    '“On or promptly following” Closing is insufficient for Buyer and its acquisition lender. The term sheet requires payoff letters from all holders at least three business days before Closing and simultaneous repayment through the funds flow. The specified holders and approximate balances are known: Cascade Mutual Bank ($28 million), Pacific Lease Corp. ($9.8 million), and Evergreen’s seller note ($4.5 million). Making delivery a Buyer closing condition protects against funding and lien-release failures and aligns the SPA with lender underwriting requirements.',
    'Buyer may retain the discretion to waive the condition or delay Closing, but the draft should not permit the transaction to close with unknown payoff amounts, unconfirmed wire instructions, or unreleased liens.'
)

add_issue(5, 'Section 4.16', 'Government contract representations and novation requirements', 'CRITICAL',
    'Environmental DD §§VI.A–C; Executed Term Sheet §§7, 12, 13; Playbook §12.2; partner instructions ¶¶113–137',
    '''(a) The Company is a party to four (4) active government contracts … with the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality, the Washington Department of Ecology, the United States Army Corps of Engineers, and the Bureau of Land Management.

(b) Each Government Contract is in full force and effect … The Company is not in material breach or default …

(c) Neither the Company nor any of its directors, officers, or employees is subject to debarment, suspension, proposed debarment, or proposed suspension …

(d) The Company has complied in all material respects with all applicable procurement Laws, regulations, and requirements …''',
    '''Replace Section 4.16 with:

Section 4.16 Government Contracts.

(a) Schedule 4.16 sets forth a true, correct, and complete list of each Government Contract, including all amendments, modifications, task orders, statements of work, and other material supplements. The Company has made available to Buyer complete copies of each Government Contract and all material correspondence with the applicable contracting agency or contracting officer concerning such Government Contract.

(b) Each Government Contract is in full force and effect and is a legal, valid, and binding obligation of the Company and, to the Knowledge of the Company, the applicable Governmental Authority. The Company is not in material breach or default under any Government Contract, and no event has occurred that, with notice or lapse of time, would constitute a material breach or default.

(c) No Government Contract is subject to any pending or, to the Knowledge of the Company, threatened termination for default or convenience, suspension, non-renewal, material modification, audit finding, cure notice, show-cause notice, or other adverse action. To the Knowledge of the Company, no contracting officer has indicated an intent to terminate, suspend, decline to renew, or materially modify any Government Contract as a result of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.

(d) Neither the Company nor any of its directors, officers, or employees is subject to debarment, suspension, proposed debarment, or proposed suspension by any Governmental Authority, and none is listed on any excluded parties list maintained by any Governmental Authority.

(e) The Company has complied in all material respects with all applicable procurement Laws, regulations, and requirements in connection with the Government Contracts. The Company has disclosed on Schedule 4.16 each notice, consent, approval, novation agreement, recognition agreement, change-of-control notification, or other submission required under any Government Contract, applicable procurement Law, the Anti-Assignment Act, 41 U.S.C. § 6305, or FAR Part 42, Subpart 42.12, in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.''',
    'The existing representations address contract status generally but do not address the principal change-of-control risk identified in diligence: the two federal contracts may require novation or recognition under FAR 42.1204, and the two state contracts may require analogous notices or approvals. The revised language confirms completeness of the contract set, absence of adverse agency action, and the required novation/consent analysis. This is necessary because the four contracts represent a material portion of revenue and loss of a contract could materially impair the platform investment.',
    'Coordinate the representation with the final Schedule 4.16 and the Government Contracts Group. Do not represent that novations have been obtained unless actually completed; the covenant and closing-condition package below uses submission/no-adverse-indication as the practical pre-closing standard.'
)

add_issue(7, 'Section 6.01(b)', 'Affiliate transactions during the interim period', 'HIGH',

    '''Section 6.01(b) contains restrictions on organizational documents, equity, indebtedness, capital expenditures, material contracts, personnel, settlements, accounting, Taxes, assets, liens, and restrictive covenants, but contains no specific restriction on transactions with Seller or Seller Affiliates.''',
    '''Add the following as new Section 6.01(b)(xiv):

(xiv) enter into, amend, modify, extend, renew, supplement, terminate, waive any rights under, make any payment or transfer any asset pursuant to, or otherwise modify or accelerate the performance of any Contract, transaction, or arrangement with Seller, any Affiliate of Seller, or any officer, director, manager, shareholder, member, partner, or family member of Seller or any Affiliate of Seller, other than (A) compensation payments to employees in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice and (B) the repayment and termination at Closing of the subordinated seller note, the Management Services Agreement, and the Tax Sharing Agreement, in each case without the prior written consent of Buyer, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. The playbook requires a specific consent right covering new, amended, extended, renewed, terminated, and paid affiliate arrangements, not merely a general material-contract restriction.',

add_issue(8, 'New Section 6.05A', 'Government contract novation / recognition cooperation', 'CRITICAL',
    'Environmental DD §§VI.B–C; Executed Term Sheet §§12 and 13; Playbook §12.2; partner instructions ¶¶113–137',
    'No specific covenant addresses the four Government Contracts, FAR 42.1204 novation requests, state change-of-control notices, or post-Closing cooperation. Section 6.05 only requires general third-party consent efforts.',
    '''Add the following as new Section 6.05A:

Section 6.05A Government Contract Notifications, Novations, and Recognition.

(a) Promptly following the date of this Agreement, and in any event sufficiently in advance of the Closing to permit agency review, Seller shall cause the Company to notify each applicable contracting officer and Governmental Authority of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement and to submit all novation, recognition, change-of-control, change-of-name, or other requests, notices, applications, and supporting materials required under any Government Contract, applicable procurement Law, the Anti-Assignment Act, 41 U.S.C. § 6305, FAR Part 42, Subpart 42.12, or analogous state requirements. Seller and the Company shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain each required novation agreement, recognition agreement, consent, or written confirmation that continued performance is permitted pending agency action.

(b) Seller shall provide Buyer with copies of all submissions, correspondence, requests for information, agency responses, and proposed novation or recognition agreements promptly after delivery or receipt, and shall not submit any material response or agree to any material modification of a Government Contract relating to the transactions contemplated by this Agreement without giving Buyer a reasonable opportunity to review and comment.

(c) As a condition to Buyer’s obligation to consummate the Closing under Section 7.02, (i) all required novation, recognition, change-of-control, and other governmental notices and requests shall have been submitted, (ii) no applicable contracting officer or Governmental Authority shall have denied any required request or indicated an intent to terminate, suspend, decline to renew, or materially modify any Government Contract as a result of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, and (iii) to the extent a contracting officer has required written confirmation for interim performance, the Company shall have received such confirmation.

(d) Following the Closing, Seller shall continue to provide reasonable cooperation, information, records, personnel access, and executed documents reasonably requested by Buyer or the Company in connection with any pending novation, recognition, change-of-control notification, or related agency process, including participation in meetings with contracting officers, until all such processes have been completed or the applicable Governmental Authority has confirmed that no further action is required.''',
    'The general consent covenant is inadequate for a stock acquisition involving two federal contracts and two state contracts that collectively represent a material revenue stream. The balanced approach recommended by the diligence memo and partner instructions requires pre-Closing submissions and best efforts, a condition that submissions have been made and no agency has issued an adverse indication, and a post-Closing cooperation tail. A hard condition requiring completed novations is reserved for discussion because FAR processing may take 60–120 days or longer and could conflict with the mid-January target and February 28 Outside Date.',
    'Client/partner decision point: whether to make receipt of completed federal novations and state consents a full condition to Closing. The proposed language is the recommended interim position pending Marcus Devereaux’s direction.'
)

add_issue(9, 'New Section 6.05B', 'Environmental permit change-of-control cooperation', 'MEDIUM',
    'Environmental DD §§V.A–B; Playbook §12.1; partner instructions ¶¶207–221',
    'No pre-Closing or post-Closing covenant addresses change-of-control notifications, approvals, or permit transfer cooperation. Section 6.05 is a general third-party-consent provision and does not identify environmental permits or provide a post-Closing tail.',
    '''Add the following as new Section 6.05B:

Section 6.05B Environmental Permit Notifications and Cooperation.

(a) Before the Closing, Seller shall cause the Company to identify each Environmental Permit for which the transactions contemplated by this Agreement require notice to, consent from, or approval by an issuing Governmental Authority, and shall prepare and submit all required notifications, applications, and requests for approval in accordance with applicable Law and the terms of such Environmental Permit. Seller and the Company shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain any approval required to be obtained before the change of control becomes effective.

(b) Seller shall provide Buyer with copies of all such filings and all material communications with the applicable Governmental Authorities and shall cooperate with Buyer in responding to requests for information and preparing supplemental submissions. Seller shall not withdraw, amend, or materially supplement any such filing without Buyer’s prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.

(c) For twelve (12) months following the Closing, or until all pending permit notifications, transfers, re-issuances, amendments, and approvals have been completed, whichever is later, Seller shall provide reasonable cooperation requested by Buyer or the Company, including executing documents, providing historical information, and participating in agency meetings or proceedings. Seller shall not be required to incur material out-of-pocket expenses without Buyer’s prior written agreement to reimburse such expenses.

(d) The Company shall maintain all Environmental Permits in full force and effect through the Closing and shall not take, or fail to take, any action reasonably expected to result in the revocation, suspension, modification, non-renewal, or material limitation of any Environmental Permit.''',
    'The stock structure preserves the permit-holding entity, but the diligence memo identifies state change-of-control notification and approval requirements in Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada. A general representation that permits currently exist does not address the regulatory process triggered by the transaction. def set_cell_shading(cell, fill):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = tcPr.find(qn('w:shd'))
    if shd is None:
        shd = OxmlElement('w:shd')
        tcPr.append(shd)
    shd.set(qn('w:fill'), fill)

def set_cell_border(cell, **kwargs):
    tc = cell._tc
    tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    tcBorders = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcBorders')
    if tcBorders is None:

        tcPr.append(tcBorders)
    for edge in ('top', 'left', 'bottom', 'right', 'insideH', 'insideV'):
        if edge in kwargs:
            edge_data = kwargs.get(edge)
            tag = 'w:{}'.format(edge)
            element = tcBorders.find(qn(tag))
            if element is None:
                element = OxmlElement(tag)
                tcBorders.append(element)
            for key in ['sz', 'val', 'color', 'space']:
                if key in edge_data:

    p = doc.add_paragraph(style=style)
    if text:
        r = p.add_run(text)
        r.bold = bold; r.italic = italic
        if color: r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(*color)
    if align is not None: p.alignment = align
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    if keep: set_keep_with_next(p)
    return p

def add_rich(paragraph, parts):
    for text, opts in parts:
        r = paragraph.add_run(text)
        if opts.get('bold'): r.bold = True
        if opts.get('italic'): r.italic = True
        if opts.get('underline'): r.underline = True
        if opts.get('color'): r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(*opts['color'])
        if opts.get('font'): r.font.name = opts['font']
        if opts.get('size'): r.font.size = Pt(opts['size'])
    return paragraph

The Company has disclosed on Schedule 4.16 each notice, consent, approval, novation agreement, recognition agreement, change-of-control notification, or other submission required under any Government Contract, applicable procurement Law, the Anti-Assignment Act, 41 U.S.C. § 6305, or FAR Part 42, Subpart 42.12, in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.''',
    'The existing representations address contract status generally but do not address the principal change-of-control risk identified in diligence: the two federal contracts may require novation or recognition under FAR 42.1204, and the two state contracts may require analogous notices or approvals. The revised language confirms completeness of the contract set, absence of adverse agency action, and the required novation/consent analysis. This is necessary because the four contracts represent a material portion of revenue and loss of a contract could materially impair the platform investment.',
    'Coordinate the representation with the final Schedule 4.16 and the Government Contracts Group. Do not represent that novations have been obtained unless actually completed; the covenant and closing-condition package below uses submission/no-adverse-indication as the practical pre-closing standard.'
)

    '''Section 6.01(b) contains restrictions on organizational documents, equity, indebtedness, capital expenditures, material contracts, personnel, settlements, accounting, Taxes, assets, liens, and restrictive covenants, but contains no specific restriction on transactions with Seller or Seller Affiliates.''',
    '''Add the following as new Section 6.01(b)(xiv):

(xiv) enter into, amend, modify, extend, renew, supplement, terminate, waive any rights under, make any payment or transfer any asset pursuant to, or otherwise modify or accelerate the performance of any Contract, transaction, or arrangement with Seller, any Affiliate of Seller, or any officer, director, manager, shareholder, member, partner, or family member of Seller or any Affiliate of Seller, other than (A) compensation payments to employees in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice and (B) the repayment and termination at Closing of the subordinated seller note, the Management Services Agreement, and the Tax Sharing Agreement, in each case without the prior written consent of Buyer, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. For the avoidance of doubt, this clause includes the Affiliate Lease and prohibits any increase in rent, extension, renewal, amendment, prepayment, or other modification of the Affiliate Lease without Buyer’s prior written consent.''',

)

add_issue(8, 'New Section 6.05A', 'Government contract novation / recognition cooperation', 'CRITICAL',
    'Environmental DD §§VI.B–C; Executed Term Sheet §§12 and 13; Playbook §12.2; partner instructions ¶¶113–137',
    'No specific covenant addresses the four Government Contracts, FAR 42.1204 novation requests, state change-of-control notices, or post-Closing cooperation. Section 6.05 only requires general third-party consent efforts.',
    '''Add the following as new Section 6.05A:

Section 6.05A Government Contract Notifications, Novations, and Recognition.

(a) Promptly following the date of this Agreement, and in any event sufficiently in advance of the Closing to permit agency review, Seller shall cause the Company to notify each applicable contracting officer and Governmental Authority of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement and to submit all novation, recognition, change-of-control, change-of-name, or other requests, notices, applications, and supporting materials required under any Government Contract, applicable procurement Law, the Anti-Assignment Act, 41 U.S.C. § 6305, FAR Part 42, Subpart 42.12, or analogous state requirements. Seller and the Company shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain each required novation agreement, recognition agreement, consent, or written confirmation that continued performance is permitted pending agency action.

(b) Seller shall provide Buyer with copies of all submissions, correspondence, requests for information, agency responses, and proposed novation or recognition agreements promptly after delivery or receipt, and shall not submit any material response or agree to any material modification of a Government Contract relating to the transactions contemplated by this Agreement without giving Buyer a reasonable opportunity to review and comment.

(c) As a condition to Buyer’s obligation to consummate the Closing under Section 7.02, (i) all required novation, recognition, change-of-control, and other governmental notices and requests shall have been submitted, (ii) no applicable contracting officer or Governmental Authority shall have denied any required request or indicated an intent to terminate, suspend, decline to renew, or materially modify any Government Contract as a result of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, and (iii) to the extent a contracting officer has required written confirmation for interim performance, the Company shall have received such confirmation.

(d) Following the Closing, Seller shall continue to provide reasonable cooperation, information, records, personnel access, and executed documents reasonably requested by Buyer or the Company in connection with any pending novation, recognition, change-of-control notification, or related agency process, including participation in meetings with contracting officers, until all such processes have been completed or the applicable Governmental Authority has confirmed that no further action is required.''',
    'The general consent covenant is inadequate for a stock acquisition involving two federal contracts and two state contracts that collectively represent a material revenue stream. The balanced approach recommended by the diligence memo and partner instructions requires pre-Closing submissions and best efforts, a condition that submissions have been made and no agency has issued an adverse indication, and a post-Closing cooperation tail. A hard condition requiring completed novations is reserved for discussion because FAR processing may take 60–120 days or longer and could conflict with the mid-January target and February 28 Outside Date.',
    'Client/partner decision point: whether to make receipt of completed federal novations and state consents a full condition to Closing. The proposed language is the recommended interim position pending Marcus Devereaux’s direction.'
)

add_issue(9, 'New Section 6.05B', 'Environmental permit change-of-control cooperation', 'MEDIUM',
    'Environmental DD §§V.A–B; Playbook §12.1; partner instructions ¶¶207–221',
    'No pre-Closing or post-Closing covenant addresses change-of-control notifications, approvals, or permit transfer cooperation. Section 6.05 is a general third-party-consent provision and does not identify environmental permits or provide a post-Closing tail.',
    '''Add the following as new Section 6.05B:

Section 6.05B Environmental Permit Notifications and Cooperation.

(a) Before the Closing, Seller shall cause the Company to identify each Environmental Permit for which the transactions contemplated by this Agreement require notice to, consent from, or approval by an issuing Governmental Authority, and shall prepare and submit all required notifications, applications, and requests for approval in accordance with applicable Law and the terms of such Environmental Permit. Seller and the Company shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain any approval required to be obtained before the change of control becomes effective.

(b) Seller shall provide Buyer with copies of all such filings and all material communications with the applicable Governmental Authorities and shall cooperate with Buyer in responding to requests for information and preparing supplemental submissions. Seller shall not withdraw, amend, or materially supplement any such filing without Buyer’s prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.

(c) For twelve (12) months following the Closing, or until all pending permit notifications, transfers, re-issuances, amendments, and approvals have been completed, whichever is later, Seller shall provide reasonable cooperation requested by Buyer or the Company, including executing documents, providing historical information, and participating in agency meetings or proceedings. Seller shall not be required to incur material out-of-pocket expenses without Buyer’s prior written agreement to reimburse such expenses.

(d) The Company shall maintain all Environmental Permits in full force and effect through the Closing and shall not take, or fail to take, any action reasonably expected to result in the revocation, suspension, modification, non-renewal, or material limitation of any Environmental Permit.''',
    'The stock structure preserves the permit-holding entity, but the diligence memo identifies state change-of-control notification and approval requirements in Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada. A general representation that permits currently exist does not address the regulatory process triggered by the transaction. The new covenant implements the playbook’s required pre-Closing and post-Closing cooperation and protects continuity of the 23-permit portfolio.',
    'Because the draft Schedule 4.15(b) lists permits with near-term expiration dates, the parties should confirm that all renewals, change-of-control notices, and approvals are reflected in the closing checklist.'
)

add_issue(10, 'New Section 6.01(a)(v) and 6.01(a)(vi)', 'Environmental insurance, active remediation, and claims notice', 'MEDIUM',
    'Environmental DD §§IV, VII; Playbook §3.3; partner instructions ¶¶207–221',
    'Section 6.01(a)(iii) generally requires the Company to maintain insurance, but the draft has no express covenant addressing environmental impairment liability insurance, the Hargrove remediation project, or prompt notice of new environmental claims or CERCLA information requests.',

(vi) continue all active remediation and environmental response projects, including the Hargrove Industrial Site project, in the ordinary course and in compliance with all applicable Environmental Laws, Governmental Orders, consent decrees, administrative agreements, remediation action plans, Government Contracts, and other governmental requirements, and not voluntarily suspend, terminate, or materially alter the scope of any such project without Buyer’s prior written consent;

(c) Seller shall cause the Company to provide Buyer written notice within five (5) Business Days after receipt of any new environmental claim, notice of violation, information request under CERCLA § 104(e), RCRA § 3007, or any analogous state-law provision, consent order, administrative complaint, or other regulatory action received during the period from the date hereof through the Closing Date.''',
    'The diligence memo identifies the $4.2 million Hargrove remediation commitment, the project-specific $10 million policy, and the broader EIL policy. It also recommends maintaining those policies and preserving active remediation work. The draft’s general insurance covenant is helpful but does not create the sector-specific protections recommended by the playbook, nor does it require prompt escalation of new environmental claims during the interim period.',
    'This is an additional diligence-driven protection. If the partner prefers not to add a separate environmental covenant package, at minimum retain the insurance-maintenance and five-business-day notice provisions.'
)

add_issue(12, 'Section 9.01', 'Environmental representation survival', 'HIGH',
    'Executed Term Sheet §8(c); Environmental DD §III.C; Playbook §§4.1–4.2 and 14; partner instructions ¶¶156–167',
    '''(b) All representations and warranties contained in this Agreement (other than the Fundamental Representations) shall survive the Closing and continue in full force and effect for a period of twelve (12) months following the Closing Date, and shall thereupon expire and be of no further force or effect.''',
    '''Replace Section 9.01(b) and add a new Section 9.01(c) as follows:

(b) All representations and warranties contained in this Agreement other than the Fundamental Representations and Environmental Representations shall survive the Closing and continue in full force and effect for a period of eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date, and shall thereupon expire and be of no further force or effect.

All covenants and agreements that are to be performed in whole prior to or at the Closing shall survive the Closing for a period of twelve (12) months following the Closing Date, except for the post-Closing cooperation covenants in Sections 6.05A and 6.05B, which shall survive for the periods stated therein.''',
    'The seller’s uniform 12-month period is inadequate for a company whose core business is environmental remediation and hazardous waste management. The DD memo identifies a Dalton Creek CERCLA exposure that may take years to crystallize and an active Hargrove project with an 18–24 month expected remaining timeline. The term sheet requires at least 36 months for environmental representations and reserves the full-statute position. The replacement preserves the agreed 18-month general survival period while separately protecting environmental representations for 36 months.',
    'Partner instruction: assume 36 months for the current markup and flag the full-applicable-statute alternative for discussion with Marcus Devereaux. Environmental survival is independent of the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, which has a 72-month survival period.'
)

add_issue(13, 'Sections 9.02 and 9.04', 'Dalton Creek Special Indemnity', 'HIGH',
    'Executed Term Sheet §9; Environmental DD §§III.A–C; Playbook §6; partner instructions ¶¶168–180',
    '''Section 9.02 contains general indemnification for breaches, covenants, Transaction Expenses, and Pre-Closing Taxes, but no Special Indemnity for Dalton Creek.

Section 9.04(a) applies the Basket to Section 9.02(a) claims other than Fundamental Representations. Section 9.04(b) applies the Indemnification Cap to non-Fundamental Representation claims. Section 9.08 provides a 36-month hold only for amounts retained as a Pending Claims Reserve relating to Fundamental Representations.''',
    '''Add the following as new Section 9.02(e):

(e) Dalton Creek Special Indemnity. From and after the Closing, Seller shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Buyer Indemnitees from and against any and all Losses arising out of, resulting from, or relating to (i) the pending information request issued by the United States Environmental Protection Agency under Section 104(e) of CERCLA concerning the Company’s former operations at the Dalton Creek disposal facility located in Clackamas County, Oregon, (ii) any investigation, notice, claim, demand, enforcement action, order, consent decree, administrative proceeding, contribution claim, cost-recovery action, or other proceeding by any Governmental Authority or third party relating to the Dalton Creek facility or such information request, and (iii) any contamination, response costs, remediation obligations, natural-resource damages, defense costs, settlement costs, penalties, fines, or other liabilities arising from or relating to the Company’s former operations, waste handling, treatment, transportation, or disposal activities at the Dalton Creek facility (the “Dalton Creek Special Indemnity”).

The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall survive the Closing until the date that is seventy-two (72) months following the Closing Date. The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall not be subject to the Basket Amount or the Indemnification Cap, and Losses indemnifiable under this Section 9.02(e) shall not be counted toward, or reduce, the Basket Amount, the Indemnification Cap, or any other limitation applicable to claims under Section 9.02(a). The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall be available from the first dollar of Loss and shall apply regardless of whether the applicable matter was disclosed to, or known by, Buyer or any of its Representatives before or after the Closing.

Add the following to Section 9.04(a):

The Basket Amount shall not apply to Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations, Fraud or willful misconduct, or the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity.

Add the following to Section 9.04(d):

The Escrow Fund shall include a portion designated for claims under the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, which portion shall remain available for such claims until the date that is thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date, subject to the terms of the Escrow Agreement. The release of such portion after that date shall not limit the Buyer Indemnitees’ right to pursue the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity directly against Seller through the 72-month survival period.''',
    'The DD memo estimates Dalton Creek exposure at $1.5 million–$6 million and identifies the EPA CERCLA §104(e) request as a precursor to possible PRP designation, investigation, cleanup, and enforcement. The term sheet expressly requires a Special Indemnity with 72-month survival, outside the general basket and cap, supported by escrow for 36 months. The draft’s omission is a direct departure from an agreed economic term and could leave a disclosed matter outside the breach-based indemnity framework.',
    'Confirm the dedicated escrow allocation with the client. The term sheet requires that a portion of the $16.125 million escrow be available for Dalton Creek claims and held for 36 months, but does not state the exact allocation. The playbook suggests sizing dedicated support at least to the low end of the estimate ($1.5 million); separate escrow is preferable if administratively feasible.'
)

add_issue(14, 'Section 9.06', 'Pro-sandbagging provision', 'CRITICAL',
    'Executed Term Sheet §8; Playbook §5.3; Environmental DD §III; partner instructions ¶¶69–86',
    '“Buyer shall not be entitled to indemnification under this Article IX with respect to any breach or inaccuracy of any representation or warranty of Seller or the Company of which Buyer or any of its Representatives had Knowledge as of the Closing Date.”',
    '''Delete Section 9.06 in its entirety and replace it with:

Section 9.06 Effect of Investigation and Knowledge. The right to indemnification or any other remedy based on the representations, warranties, covenants, and obligations set forth in this Agreement shall not be affected by any investigation conducted by or on behalf of Buyer or any of its Representatives or by any knowledge acquired (or capable of being acquired) by Buyer or any of its Representatives at any time, whether before or after the execution and delivery of this Agreement or the Closing Date, with respect to the accuracy or inaccuracy of, or compliance with, any such representation, warranty, covenant, or obligation. No claim for indemnification under this Article IX shall be defeated, diminished, or otherwise affected by reason of any investigation, knowledge, notice, or information of or available to Buyer or any of its Representatives, regardless of whether such investigation, knowledge, notice, or information was obtained before or after the Closing.''',
    'The draft’s express anti-sandbagging clause is a dealbreaker and would penalize Buyer for conducting the extensive financial, legal, environmental, regulatory, and operational diligence expected in this transaction. The playbook requires an affirmative pro-sandbagging clause because representations and warranties are a negotiated contractual allocation of risk independent of Buyer’s diligence knowledge. This protection is especially important for the Dalton Creek matter and other environmental issues identified before Closing.',
    'Do not leave a knowledge-based limitation elsewhere in the SPA, Disclosure Schedules, or Escrow Agreement. The clause should apply to actual, constructive, imputed, or otherwise available knowledge.'
)

    '''(a) General Release … on the date that is eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date …

(b) Final Release … retained as a Pending Claims Reserve … until final resolution or the date that is thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date with respect to claims relating to Fundamental Representations.''',

    'The draft’s 36-month reserve applies only to Fundamental Representation claims, not to the required Dalton Creek Special Indemnity. The term sheet and diligence recommendations require escrow support for Special Indemnity claims for 36 months, while the underlying Special Indemnity survives 72 months. add_heading('A. Dalton Creek disclosure discrepancy — immediate factual correction', level=2)
add_label_para('Seller’s draft issue: ', 'Schedule 4.15(d), Item 2 states that the Dalton Creek site is in Lane County and that the EPA information request is dated June 12, 2025. The diligence memo and executed term sheet identify the site as located in Clackamas County, Oregon and the request as dated February 12, 2025. The term sheet also describes the Dalton Creek Facility as the former operations site covered by the Special Indemnity.', fill='FCE4D6')
add_label_para('Proposed schedule replacement: ', '', fill='E2F0D9')
add_code('''2. Dalton Creek Disposal Facility — Clackamas County, Oregon.

The Company received an information request from the United States Environmental Protection Agency, Region 10, dated February 12, 2025, pursuant to Section 104(e) of CERCLA, 42 U.S.C. § 9604(e), regarding the Company’s former operations at the Dalton Creek disposal facility located in Clackamas County, Oregon (the “Dalton Creek Facility”). The information request seeks information regarding the types, quantities, characterization, handling, transportation, and disposal of hazardous wastes associated with the Company’s former operations at the Dalton Creek Facility. As of the date hereof, no formal enforcement action, notice of potential responsibility, unilateral administrative order, consent decree, or lawsuit has been issued or filed against the Company in connection with the Dalton Creek Facility. 1: **ASHFORD, PENNINGTON & YATES LLP**
2: 
3: **PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL --- ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT**

5: **MARKUP MEMORANDUM**
6: 
7: **Seller's Draft Stock Purchase Agreement**
8: 
9: *Acquisition of Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc.*
10: 
11:   ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
12:   **To**                              Elena Vasquez-Moreno, Partner; Jonathan Kreider, Senior Associate
13:   ----------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
14:   **From**                            Buyer's deal team --- SPA review memorandum
15: 
16:   **Date**                            October 29, 2025
17: 
18:   **Transaction**                     Whitmore Capital Partners LLC / Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc.
19: 
20:   **Documents reviewed**              Seller's draft SPA dated October 22, 2025; executed term sheet dated September 10, 2025; M&A Playbook (v4.2); Environmental DD Summary dated October 18, 2025; partner instructions dated October 23, 2025
21: 
22:   **Purpose**                         Buyer-side, article-by-article markup memorandum with draft-ready replacement language and track-changes comments
23:   ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
24: 
25: **Confidentiality:** This memorandum is prepared for the exclusive use of the buyer's legal team and client in connection with Project Cascade. It contains attorney work product and should not be circulated outside the intended deal team.
26: 
27: This memorandum is organized by SPA article and section. Each item identifies the seller's draft language, provides full proposed contract language suitable for a redline, includes a concise rationale tied to the term sheet, playbook, or diligence materials, and assigns a priority level.
28: 
29: # Executive Summary
30: 
31: The seller's draft is materially seller-favorable and departs from the executed term sheet and buyer playbook on several negotiated risk-allocation provisions. The most significant issues are the MAE carve-outs, anti-sandbagging language, earnout operating restrictions, omission of a Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, the 20% indemnification cap, the one-year environmental survival period, debt payoff mechanics, and the absence of a government-contract novation framework. The draft also requires targeted additions for environmental permit notifications, R&W insurance subrogation, affiliate transactions, and the agreed non-compete scope.
32: 
33: The recommended markup is intentionally disciplined: it leaves the 1% true-deductible basket, CEO/CFO actual-knowledge qualifier, 10-business-day good-standing certificate timing, and Delaware governing law unchanged, consistent with the partner's instructions and the playbook's "do not mark up" guidance.
34: 
35: ## Priority Matrix
36: 
37:   -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
38:   **\#**            **Issue / SPA location**                      **Priority**      **Buyer position**
39:   ----------------- --------------------------------------------- ----------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
40:   1                 MAE definition --- §1.01                      **CRITICAL**      Add disproportionate-impact qualifiers to industry and Environmental Law carve-outs; preserve exposure to target-specific regulatory harm.
41: 
42:   2                 Earnout --- §2.05                             **CRITICAL**      Delete affirmative "past practice / maximize" covenants; use only the primary-purpose negative covenant and conform timing to the term sheet.
43: 
44:   3                 Government contracts --- §§4.16, 6.05, 7.02   **CRITICAL**      Add novation/recognition representations, pre-closing submissions and best efforts, post-closing cooperation, and a balanced closing condition.
45: 
46:   4                 Environmental survival --- §9.01              **HIGH**          Carve environmental representations out of the 12-month period and extend to at least 36 months; preserve full-statute alternative.
47: 
48:   5                 Dalton Creek Special Indemnity --- Art. IX    **HIGH**          Add 72-month, first-dollar, uncapped Special Indemnity; maintain escrow support for 36 months.
49: 
50:   6                 Affiliate transactions --- §6.01              **HIGH**          Require Buyer's prior written consent for new, amended, extended, renewed, terminated, or accelerated affiliate arrangements.
51: 
52:   7                 Debt payoff --- §§2.03, 2.08, 7.02            **HIGH**          Require payoff letters at least three business days before Closing and simultaneous repayment through the funds flow.
53: 
54:   8                 Indemnification cap --- §§1.01, 9.04          **HIGH**          Replace 20% / \$43.0 million cap with 12.5% / \$26.875 million; preserve Special Indemnity outside the cap.
55: 
56:   9                 Permit cooperation --- §§4.15, 6.05           **MEDIUM**        Add pre- and post-closing change-of-control notification / approval cooperation for 23 permits across four states.
57: 
58:   10                R&W insurance --- Art. X                      **MEDIUM**        Add insurer subrogation waiver in favor of Seller and affiliates, except for Seller fraud.
59: 
60:   11                Non-compete --- §6.09                         **MEDIUM**        Conform to 3 years, OR/WA/CA/NV, environmental remediation and hazardous waste management only.
61: 
62:   12                Sandbagging --- §9.06                         **CRITICAL**      Strike anti-sandbagging provision and replace with affirmative pro-sandbagging language.
63:   -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
64: 
65: Note: The term "Critical" is used where the partner instructions identify a non-negotiable or dealbreaker position. The playbook treats several "High" items, including environmental survival and the general cap, as critical sector requirements; the memorandum preserves the partner's requested negotiation labels while noting the playbook support.
66: 
67: ## Items Intentionally Left Unchanged
68: 
69: - Basket: \$2,150,000, equal to 1% of Base Enterprise Value, as a true deductible. This is within the playbook's 0.75%--1.0% range and matches Term Sheet §8.
70: 
71: - Knowledge: actual knowledge of Patricia Huang and Robert Merrill, without constructive knowledge. This is acceptable for a 340-employee target under Playbook §§11.1--11.2.
72: 
73: - Good-standing certificates dated within 10 business days of Closing. This is within the playbook's 5--10 business-day range.
74: 
75: - Delaware governing law. Both Buyer and Seller are Delaware entities and the provision is consistent with the playbook.
76: 
77: # Detailed Article-by-Article Markup
78: 
79: The following provisions are drafted as replacement text or insertions. Bracketed section references should be conformed to the final numbering after the parties incorporate the additions.
80: 
81: ## Article I --- Definitions
82: 
83: ## 1. Section 1.01 --- Material Adverse Effect definition (CRITICAL)
84: 
85: **Sources:** Executed Term Sheet §12(c); Playbook §§2.1--2.2 and 14; Environmental DD §§III--VI; partner instructions ¶¶52--67
86: 
87: **Seller's draft language:**
88: 
89: > "Material Adverse Effect" means any event, change, effect, development, state of facts, condition, circumstance, or occurrence that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or results of operations of the Company, or (b) the ability of Seller to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement; provided, however, that none of the following, individually or in the aggregate, shall be deemed to constitute, or shall be taken into account in determining whether there has been or would reasonably be expected to be, a Material Adverse Effect: (i) changes in general economic, financial, credit, securities market, or political conditions in the United States or globally; (ii) changes in conditions generally affecting the environmental services industry; (iii) changes in Environmental Laws or regulations; (iv) changes in GAAP or applicable Law (other than Environmental Laws, which are addressed in clause (iii) above); (v) acts of war ... epidemics, pandemics, earthquakes, hurricanes, tornados, floods, or other natural disasters or acts of God; (vi) the announcement or pendency of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement ...; (vii) any action taken by the Company at the express written request or with the express written consent of Buyer; and (viii) any failure by the Company to meet any internal or external projections ...
90: 
91: **Proposed buyer redline / replacement language:**
92: 
93: > "Material Adverse Effect" means any event, change, effect, development, state of facts, condition, circumstance, or occurrence that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or results of operations of the Company, or (b) the ability of Seller to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement; provided, however, that none of the following, individually or in the aggregate, shall be deemed to constitute, or shall be taken into account in determining whether there has been or would reasonably be expected to be, a Material Adverse Effect: (i) changes in general economic, financial, credit, securities market, or political conditions in the United States or globally; (ii) changes in conditions generally affecting the environmental services industry; (iii) changes in Environmental Laws or regulations; (iv) changes in GAAP or applicable Law (other than Environmental Laws, which are addressed in clause (iii) above); (v) acts of war (whether or not declared), armed hostilities, sabotage, terrorism, military actions, or any escalation or worsening thereof, epidemics, pandemics, earthquakes, hurricanes, tornados, floods, or other natural disasters or acts of God; (vi) the announcement or pendency of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, including any impact on relationships with customers, suppliers, employees, or Governmental Authorities; (vii) any action taken by the Company at the express written request or with the express written consent of Buyer; and (viii) any failure by the Company to meet any internal or external projections, forecasts, or estimates of revenue, earnings, or other financial performance metrics for any period; provided, further, that, with respect to clauses (i) through (vi), such change, effect, event, or development shall be taken into account in determining whether a Material Adverse Effect has occ... (line truncated to 2000 chars)
94: 
95: **Track-changes comment / rationale:** The draft's industry-specific and Environmental Law carve-outs omit the required disproportionate-impact exception. Cascadia's value is concentrated in environmental remediation, hazardous waste management, permits, and government contracts; therefore, an industry-wide or regulatory development can materially affect this target even if it is characterized as general. The revised language preserves customary carve-outs but prevents those carve-outs from insulating target-specific or disproportionate harm, including a regulatory development affecting Cascadia's disposal, remediation, or permit profile. This is the playbook's stated non-negotiable position and is particularly important given the Dalton Creek and permit risks identified in diligence.
96: 
97: **Negotiation / implementation note:** Conform "Company and its Subsidiaries" to the SPA's defined terms; if the Company has no subsidiaries, "Company, taken as a whole" is acceptable. Do not add a litigation carve-out; the playbook cautions against excluding environmental claims from the MAE analysis.
98: 
99: ## 2. Section 1.01 --- Indemnification Cap definition (HIGH)
100: 
101: **Sources:** Executed Term Sheet §8; Playbook §5.1; partner instructions ¶¶143--155
102: 
103: **Seller's draft language:**
104: 
105: > "Indemnification Cap" means Forty-Three Million Dollars (\$43,000,000), which is equal to twenty percent (20%) of the Base Enterprise Value.
106: 
107: **Proposed buyer redline / replacement language:**
108: 
109: > "Indemnification Cap" means Twenty-Six Million Eight Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$26,875,000), which is equal to twelve and one-half percent (12.5%) of the Base Enterprise Value.
110: 
111: **Track-changes comment / rationale:** The seller's 20% / \$43 million cap directly contradicts the executed term sheet, which fixes the general cap at 12.5% of the \$215 million Base Enterprise Value, or \$26.875 million. The playbook instructs that the executed term sheet controls economic terms and that a deviation must be corrected without treating it as a drafting gray area.
112: 
113: **Negotiation / implementation note:** The cap is for Losses arising from breaches of non-Fundamental Representations. Fundamental Representation liability remains subject to the Purchase Price cap, and the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity must remain outside the general cap.
114: 
115: ## Article II --- Purchase and Sale; Purchase Price
116: 
117: ## 3. Section 2.05 --- Earnout covenant and financial mechanics (CRITICAL)
118: 
119: **Sources:** Executed Term Sheet §5; Playbook §§7.1--7.2; partner instructions ¶¶88--111
120: 
121: **Seller's draft language:**
122: 
123: > \(c\) Within sixty (60) days after the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall prepare and deliver to Seller a written statement ... setting forth Buyer's good-faith calculation of Adjusted EBITDA ...
124: >
125: > \(d\) From and after the Closing Date through the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall, and shall cause the Company to, operate the business of the Company in a manner consistent with past practice and in good faith to maximize the Earnout Payment. ... Buyer shall cause the Company to maintain substantially the same level of personnel, equipment, and other resources ... and shall not divert or redirect any contracts, customers, revenues, or business opportunities ...
126: >
127: > \(e\) Any Earnout Payment ... shall be paid ... within ten (10) Business Days after the final determination of Adjusted EBITDA ...
128: 
129: **Proposed buyer redline / replacement language:**
130: 
131: > Replace Section 2.05(c), (d), and (e) in their entirety with the following:
132: >
133: > \(c\) Within forty-five (45) days following the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall prepare and deliver to Seller a written statement (the "Earnout Statement") setting forth Buyer's good-faith calculation of Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period and the resulting Earnout Payment, if any, together with reasonable supporting detail. Seller shall have thirty (30) days following receipt of the Earnout Statement to review the Earnout Statement and deliver a written notice of objection specifying in reasonable detail each disputed item and the amount Seller believes to be correct. Any dispute not resolved by the Parties within twenty (20) Business Days after delivery of such notice shall be submitted to the Independent Accountant under Section 2.04(c), whose determination shall be final and binding absent manifest error.
134: >
135: > \(d\) Following the Closing, Buyer shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, take any action with the primary purpose of avoiding or reducing the Earnout Payment. For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this Section 2.05(d) shall restrict Buyer's right to operate, integrate, restructure, or otherwise manage the Company and its business in Buyer's sole discretion, including the right to make capital expenditure decisions, change pricing or compensation, make strategic investments, acquire or dispose of businesses or assets, reorganize the Company or its operations, allocate resources, or take any other operational action, and no such action shall constitute a breach of this Section 2.05(d) unless taken with the primary purpose of avoiding or reducing the Earnout Payment. Buyer shall have no affirmative obligation to operate the Company in any particular manner, to maximize the Earnout Payment, to maintain the Company as a separate entity, to maintain any particular level of personnel, equipment, capital expenditures, or resources, to retain any employee, or to refrain from diverting or redirecting contracts, customers, revenues, or business opportunities, in each case except to the extent an action is taken with the primary purpose of avoiding or reducing the Earnout Payment.
136: >
137: > \(e\) Any Earnout Payment determined to be payable pursuant to this Section 2.05 shall be paid by Buyer to Seller within sixty (60) days following the end of the Earnout Period, subject to final determination under this Section 2.05, by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Seller. For U.S. federal income tax purposes, the Parties agree to treat any Earnout Payment as an adjustment to the Purchase Price.
138: 
139: **Track-changes comment / rationale:** The seller's affirmative operating obligations would effectively give Seller veto rights over Buyer's platform integration, restructuring, personnel, capital allocation, and bolt-on strategy through December 31, 2026. The playbook permits only a narrow negative covenant against actions taken with the primary purpose of avoiding or reducing the earnout. The economic thresholds in the draft are correct (\$25 million maximum; \$38 million full-payment threshold; \$32 million floor; linear interpolation), but the timing is not: the term sheet requires the calculation within 45 days and payment within 60 days after the Measurement Period. The replacement language preserves the agreed economics and restores Buyer's operational flexibility.
140: 
141: **Negotiation / implementation note:** Confirm that the final Exhibit D includes the agreed Adjusted EBITDA methodology and add-backs for buyer-directed integration costs, restructuring charges, non-recurring items, and post-closing affiliate/corporate allocations not charged consistently before Closing.
142: 
143: ## 4. Sections 2.03(d), 2.08(a), and 7.02 --- Debt payoff letters, funds flow, and closing condition (HIGH)
144: 
145: **Sources:** Executed Term Sheet §6; Playbook §9.2; partner instructions ¶¶193--205; Clearwater Environmental Lending Corp. financing context

147: **Seller's draft language:**

150: >
151: > Section 2.08(a): Seller's closing deliverables do not include payoff letters.
152: >
153: > Section 7.02: Buyer's conditions do not include delivery of payoff letters.
154: 
155: **Proposed buyer redline / replacement language:**
156: 
157: > Replace Section 2.03(d) with:
158: >

**PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL --- ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT**
**MARKUP MEMORANDUM**
**Seller's Draft Stock Purchase Agreement**
*Acquisition of Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc.*
**To**                              Elena Vasquez-Moreno, Partner; Jonathan Kreider, Senior Associate
**From**                            Buyer's deal team --- SPA review memorandum
**Date**                            October 29, 2025
**Transaction**                     Whitmore Capital Partners LLC / Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc.

**Documents reviewed**              Seller's draft SPA dated October 22, 2025; executed term sheet dated September 10, 2025; M&A Playbook (v4.2); Environmental DD Summary dated October 18, 2025; partner instructions dated October 23, 2025
**Purpose**                         Buyer-side, article-by-article markup memorandum with draft-ready replacement language and track-changes comments

**Confidentiality:** This memorandum is prepared for the exclusive use of the buyer's legal team and client in connection with Project Cascade. It contains attorney work product and should not be circulated outside the intended deal team.

This memorandum is organized by SPA article and section. Each item identifies the seller's draft language, provides full proposed contract language suitable for a redline, includes a concise rationale tied to the term sheet, playbook, or diligence materials, and assigns a priority level.
# Executive Summary

The seller's draft is materially seller-favorable and departs from the executed term sheet and buyer playbook on several negotiated risk-allocation provisions. The most significant issues are the MAE carve-outs, anti-sandbagging language, earnout operating restrictions, omission of a Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, the 20% indemnification cap, the one-year environmental survival period, debt payoff mechanics, and the absence of a government-contract novation framework. The draft also requires targeted additions for environmental permit notifications, R&W insurance subrogation, affiliate transactions, and the agreed non-compete scope.

The recommended markup is intentionally disciplined: it leaves the 1% true-deductible basket, CEO/CFO actual-knowledge qualifier, 10-business-day good-standing certificate timing, and Delaware governing law unchanged, consistent with the partner's instructions and the playbook's "do not mark up" guidance.
## Priority Matrix
**\#**            **Issue / SPA location**                      **Priority**      **Buyer position**

**Proposed buyer redline / replacement language:**
> Replace Section 2.05(c), (d), and (e) in their entirety with the following:

> \(c\) Within forty-five (45) days following the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall prepare and deliver to Seller a written statement (the "Earnout Statement") setting forth Buyer's good-faith calculation of Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period and the resulting Earnout Payment, if any, together with reasonable supporting detail.
