> Section 7.02 does not include delivery of an executed employment agreement for Patricia Huang. Exhibit B states: "The Employment Agreement for Patricia Huang shall provide for her continued service as Chief Executive Officer of the Company following the Closing, on terms and conditions to be agreed upon by Buyer and Ms. Huang."
**Proposed buyer redline / replacement language:**
> Add the following as new Section 7.02(i):

> \(i\) Buyer shall have received an executed employment agreement between the Company and Patricia Huang, in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to Buyer, providing for her continued service as Chief Executive Officer of the Company following the Closing.
> Add the following as new Section 2.08(a)(xi):
> \(xi\) the employment agreement between the Company and Patricia Huang described in Section 7.02(i), duly executed by Ms. Huang and the Company.

**Track-changes comment / rationale:** The executed term sheet expressly makes Patricia Huang's employment agreement a Buyer closing condition. The draft relegates the agreement to an exhibit "to be negotiated separately" and omits it from both the closing deliverables and the Buyer conditions. This is a material implementation gap, particularly because Patricia Huang is one of the two individuals whose actual knowledge is used for the Company's Knowledge qualifier and she is identified as the CEO/key employee.

**Negotiation / implementation note:** The form should be circulated and agreed before the closing checklist is finalized. This is separate from the 12 PE-licensed employees, for whom the SPA contains a good-standing representation but no retention covenant.
## Article IX --- Indemnification
## 12. Section 9.01 --- Environmental representation survival (HIGH)
**Sources:** Executed Term Sheet §8(c); Environmental DD §III.C; Playbook §§4.1--4.2 and 14; partner instructions ¶¶156--167
**Seller's draft language:**

> \(b\) All representations and warranties contained in this Agreement (other than the Fundamental Representations) shall survive the Closing and continue in full force and effect for a period of twelve (12) months following the Closing Date, and shall thereupon expire and be of no further force or effect.
**Proposed buyer redline / replacement language:**
> Replace Section 9.01(b) and add a new Section 9.01(c) as follows:

> \(b\) All representations and warranties contained in this Agreement other than the Fundamental Representations and Environmental Representations shall survive the Closing and continue in full force and effect for a period of eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date, and shall thereupon expire and be of no further force or effect.

> \(c\) The representations and warranties set forth in Section 4.15 (Environmental Matters), Section 4.16 (Government Contracts) to the extent relating to environmental or regulatory compliance, and any other representation or warranty expressly relating to Environmental Laws, Environmental Permits, Hazardous Substances, environmental insurance, environmental remediation, or environmental liabilities (collectively, the "Environmental Representations") shall survive the Closing and continue in full force and effect until the date that is thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date. Buyer reserves the right to seek survival of Environmental Representations through the full applicable statute of limitations, including any extension or tolling period, and nothing in this Section 9.01(c) shall limit any claim timely asserted under the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity.

> \(d\) All covenants and agreements of the Parties contained in this Agreement that by their terms are to be performed in whole or in part after the Closing shall survive the Closing in accordance with their terms. All covenants and agreements that are to be performed in whole prior to or at the Closing shall survive the Closing for a period of twelve (12) months following the Closing Date, except for the post-Closing cooperation covenants in Sections 6.05A and 6.05B, which shall survive for the periods stated therein.

**Track-changes comment / rationale:** The seller's uniform 12-month period is inadequate for a company whose core business is environmental remediation and hazardous waste management. The DD memo identifies a Dalton Creek CERCLA exposure that may take years to crystallize and an active Hargrove project with an 18--24 month expected remaining timeline. The term sheet requires at least 36 months for environmental representations and reserves the full-statute position. The replacement preserves the agreed 18-month general survival period while separately protecting environmental representations for 36 months.

**Negotiation / implementation note:** Partner instruction: assume 36 months for the current markup and flag the full-applicable-statute alternative for discussion with Marcus Devereaux. Environmental survival is independent of the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, which has a 72-month survival period.
## 13. Sections 9.02 and 9.04 --- Dalton Creek Special Indemnity (HIGH)
**Sources:** Executed Term Sheet §9; Environmental DD §§III.A--C; Playbook §6; partner instructions ¶¶168--180
**Seller's draft language:**
> Section 9.02 contains general indemnification for breaches, covenants, Transaction Expenses, and Pre-Closing Taxes, but no Special Indemnity for Dalton Creek.

> Section 9.04(a) applies the Basket to Section 9.02(a) claims other than Fundamental Representations. Section 9.04(b) applies the Indemnification Cap to non-Fundamental Representation claims. Section 9.08 provides a 36-month hold only for amounts retained as a Pending Claims Reserve relating to Fundamental Representations.
**Proposed buyer redline / replacement language:**
> Add the following as new Section 9.02(e):

> \(e\) Dalton Creek Special Indemnity. From and after the Closing, Seller shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Buyer Indemnitees from and against any and all Losses arising out of, resulting from, or relating to (i) the pending information request issued by the United States Environmental Protection Agency under Section 104(e) of CERCLA concerning the Company's former operations at the Dalton Creek disposal facility located in Clackamas County, Oregon, (ii) any investigation, notice, claim, demand, enforcement action, order, consent decree, administrative proceeding, contribution claim, cost-recovery action, or other proceeding by any Governmental Authority or third party relating to the Dalton Creek facility or such information request, and (iii) any contamination, response costs, remediation obligations, natural-resource damages, defense costs, settlement costs, penalties, fines, or other liabilities arising from or relating to the Company's former operations, waste handling, treatment, transportation, or disposal activities at the Dalton Creek facility (the "Dalton Creek Special Indemnity").

> The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall survive the Closing until the date that is seventy-two (72) months following the Closing Date. The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall not be subject to the Basket Amount or the Indemnification Cap, and Losses indemnifiable under this Section 9.02(e) shall not be counted toward, or reduce, the Basket Amount, the Indemnification Cap, or any other limitation applicable to claims under Section 9.02(a). The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall be available from the first dollar of Loss and shall apply regardless of whether the applicable matter was disclosed to, or known by, Buyer or any of its Representatives before or after the Closing.
> Add the following to Section 9.04(a):
> The Basket Amount shall not apply to Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations, Fraud or willful misconduct, or the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity.
> Add the following to Section 9.04(d):

> The Escrow Fund shall include a portion designated for claims under the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, which portion shall remain available for such claims until the date that is thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date, subject to the terms of the Escrow Agreement. The release of such portion after that date shall not limit the Buyer Indemnitees' right to pursue the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity directly against Seller through the 72-month survival period.

**Track-changes comment / rationale:** The DD memo estimates Dalton Creek exposure at \$1.5 million--\$6 million and identifies the EPA CERCLA §104(e) request as a precursor to possible PRP designation, investigation, cleanup, and enforcement. The term sheet expressly requires a Special Indemnity with 72-month survival, outside the general basket and cap, supported by escrow for 36 months. The draft's omission is a direct departure from an agreed economic term and could leave a disclosed matter outside the breach-based indemnity framework.

405: ## 14. Section 9.06 --- Pro-sandbagging provision (CRITICAL)
406: 
407: **Sources:** Executed Term Sheet §8; Playbook §5.3; Environmental DD §III; partner instructions ¶¶69--86
408: 
409: **Seller's draft language:**
410: 
411: > "Buyer shall not be entitled to indemnification under this Article IX with respect to any breach or inaccuracy of any representation or warranty of Seller or the Company of which Buyer or any of its Representatives had Knowledge as of the Closing Date."

415: > Delete Section 9.06 in its entirety and replace it with:
416: >
417: > Section 9.06 Effect of Investigation and Knowledge. The right to indemnification or any other remedy based on the representations, warranties, covenants, and obligations set forth in this Agreement shall not be affected by any investigation conducted by or on behalf of Buyer or any of its Representatives or by any knowledge acquired (or capable of being acquired) by Buyer or any of its Representatives at any time, whether before or after the execution and delivery of this Agreement or the Closing Date, with respect to the accuracy or inaccuracy of, or compliance with, any such representation, warranty, covenant, or obligation. The playbook requires an affirmative pro-sandbagging clause because representations and warranties are a negotiated contractual allocation of risk independent of Buyer's diligence knowledge. This protection is especially important for the Dalton Creek matter and other environmental issues identified before Closing.

428: 
429: > \(a\) General Release ... on the date that is eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date ...
430: >
431: > \(b\) Final Release ... retained as a Pending Claims Reserve ... until final resolution or the date that is thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date with respect to claims relating to Fundamental Representations.

435: > Replace Section 9.08(b) with:
436: >
437: > \(b\) Final Release. With respect to any portion of the Escrow Fund retained as a Pending Claims Reserve, including any portion designated for claims under the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, such amounts shall continue to be held in the Escrow Fund until (i) final resolution of the applicable pending claim in accordance with this Article IX or (ii) the date that is thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date with respect to claims relating to Fundamental Representations or the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity. For the avoidance of doubt, release of any Escrow Fund after the applicable release date shall not limit any Buyer Indemnitee's right to pursue Seller directly for Losses under the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity through its 72-month survival period.

The term sheet and diligence recommendations require escrow support for Special Indemnity claims for 36 months, while the underlying Special Indemnity survives 72 months. The revised text coordinates the escrow schedule with the negotiated risk allocation without converting escrow into a cap on recovery.

445: ## 16. New Section 10.13 --- R&W insurance subrogation waiver (MEDIUM)

451: > The draft contains no provision addressing Buyer's representations and warranties insurance policy, Granite Ridge Underwriters, or waiver of insurer subrogation rights against Seller and its affiliates.

454: 
455: > Add the following as new Section 10.13:
456: >
457: > Section 10.13 R&W Insurance; Subrogation Waiver. Buyer shall obtain and maintain a representations and warranties insurance policy in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement (the "R&W Insurance Policy") and shall cause the R&W Insurance Policy to provide that the insurer thereunder irrevocably waives, and shall not exercise or pursue, any right of subrogation or other right of recovery against Seller or any of Seller's Affiliates, directors, officers, employees, agents, or Representatives with respect to any claim made by Buyer or any Buyer Indemnitee under the R&W Insurance Policy, except to the extent such claim arises from or relates to actual Fraud by Seller. Buyer shall not amend, modify, terminate, or waive the R&W Insurance Policy in a manner that would adversely affect Seller's rights under this Section 10.13 without Seller's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. The obligations of Buyer under this Section 10.13 shall survive the Closing for the term of the R&W Insurance Policy.

The draft is silent. The provision is standard market risk allocation and should be included without reducing Seller's direct obligations under the SPA or changing the cap, basket, or escrow.

461: **Negotiation / implementation note:** Buyer should confirm the final policy form includes the waiver and that the fraud exception is limited to actual Seller fraud, consistent with the term sheet.

465: ## 17. Section 6.09(a) --- Non-competition covenant scope (MEDIUM)
466: 
467: **Sources:** Executed Term Sheet §11; Playbook §10.1; partner instructions ¶¶237--246
468: 
469: **Seller's draft language:**
470: 
471: > \(a\) For a period of five (5) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, engage in, own, manage, operate, control, participate in, consult with, render services for, or in any manner be connected with any business anywhere in the United States; provided that ... passive public-company investment and performance under the Transaction Documents are permitted.

473: **Proposed buyer redline / replacement language:**
474: 
475: > Replace Section 6.09(a) with:

477: > \(a\) Non-Competition. For a period of three (3) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its controlled Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, engage in, own, manage, operate, finance, control, or participate in the ownership, management, operation, financing, or control of any business engaged in the provision of environmental remediation services or hazardous waste management services, in each case in the States of Oregon, Washington, California, or Nevada; provided that this Section 6.09(a) shall not restrict Seller or its Affiliates from (i) conducting their construction, timber, and other businesses as conducted as of the Closing Date, (ii) holding, solely as a passive investment, less than five percent (5%) of the outstanding equity securities of any publicly traded entity, or (iii) performing environmental-related activities that are incidental to and performed solely in connection with Seller's construction or timber operations, including erosion control, stormwater management, and environmental compliance activities at Seller's own sites. The term sheet fixes a three-year period, four-state geography, and the specific business scope of environmental remediation and hazardous waste management services. The revised language tracks those negotiated limits and preserves the agreed carve-outs.

Partner instructions specifically require narrowing the non-compete; confirm whether the client also wants the non-solicit reduced from three years to the term sheet's two years and limited to Company employees.

487: ## A. Dalton Creek disclosure discrepancy --- immediate factual correction
488: 
489: **Seller's draft issue:** Schedule 4.15(d), Item 2 states that the Dalton Creek site is in Lane County and that the EPA information request is dated June 12, 2025. The diligence memo and executed term sheet identify the site as located in Clackamas County, Oregon and the request as dated February 12, 2025. The term sheet also describes the Dalton Creek Facility as the former operations site covered by the Special Indemnity.

491: **Proposed schedule replacement:**
492: 
493: > 2\. Dalton Creek Disposal Facility --- Clackamas County, Oregon.

The information request seeks information regarding the types, quantities, characterization, handling, transportation, and disposal of hazardous wastes associated with the Company's former operations at the Dalton Creek Facility. As of the date hereof, no formal enforcement action, notice of potential responsibility, unilateral administrative order, consent decree, or lawsuit has been issued or filed against the Company in connection with the Dalton Creek Facility. The Company has engaged outside environmental counsel to assist in responding to the information request. Outside environmental counsel estimates the Company's potential liability, if designated as a potentially responsible party, at between \$1,500,000 and \$6,000,000, depending on the scope of remediation and allocation of responsibility among potentially responsible parties.

The Special Indemnity and all cross-references should use one consistent defined term and factual description.

Confirm the project schedule, remaining cost estimate (\$4.2 million), DEQ contract/task order, and insurance status. This affects the environmental survival and interim covenant analysis.

505: - Term Sheet §17 refers to a Confidentiality Agreement dated July 12, 2025; SPA §6.03 refers to a Mutual Confidentiality Agreement dated June 20, 2025. Confirm which agreement governs and conform the recital/reference before execution.
506: 
507: - The term sheet lists Buyer's address as 200 South Wacker Drive, Suite 3100, Chicago, Illinois 60606; SPA §10.01 lists 210 South Wacker Drive. Confirm the correct notice address.

The term sheet identifies a \$125 million Clearwater Environmental Lending Corp. financing commitment but does not identify Fund IV. This is a factual and execution issue rather than a requested economic markup.
512: 
513: ## E. Environmental permit schedule requires action tracking
514: 
515: Schedule 4.15(b) includes several permits with expirations near the anticipated Closing or shortly thereafter, including the Oregon UST permit, Oregon remediation contractor license, Washington Ecology contractor license, and California CUPA permit. Prepare a permit action tracker identifying the issuing agency, change-of-control notice deadline, approval requirement, renewal date, responsible party, filing status, and evidence of submission. The SPA covenant should be cross-checked against that tracker.

This is an additional diligence recommendation, not a current partner priority. Consider requiring Seller to disclose any notice of resignation or threatened departure by the 12 listed license holders and adding a covenant to use commercially reasonable efforts to retain them through Closing. Buyer should assess whether separate employment or retention agreements are needed for critical PE-licensed personnel.

**Sources:** Executed Term Sheet §10; Playbook §§8.1--8.2; partner instructions ¶¶223--235
**Seller's draft language:**

> The draft contains no provision addressing Buyer's representations and warranties insurance policy, Granite Ridge Underwriters, or waiver of insurer subrogation rights against Seller and its affiliates.
**Proposed buyer redline / replacement language:**
> Add the following as new Section 10.13:

> Section 10.13 R&W Insurance; Subrogation Waiver. Buyer shall obtain and maintain a representations and warranties insurance policy in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement (the "R&W Insurance Policy") and shall cause the R&W Insurance Policy to provide that the insurer thereunder irrevocably waives, and shall not exercise or pursue, any right of subrogation or other right of recovery against Seller or any of Seller's Affiliates, directors, officers, employees, agents, or Representatives with respect to any claim made by Buyer or any Buyer Indemnitee under the R&W Insurance Policy, except to the extent such claim arises from or relates to actual Fraud by Seller. Buyer shall not amend, modify, terminate, or waive the R&W Insurance Policy in a manner that would adversely affect Seller's rights under this Section 10.13 without Seller's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. The obligations of Buyer under this Section 10.13 shall survive the Closing for the term of the R&W Insurance Policy.

**Track-changes comment / rationale:** The term sheet acknowledges Buyer's R&W insurance placement and requires a subrogation waiver in favor of Seller and its related parties, except for Seller fraud. The draft is silent. The provision is standard market risk allocation and should be included without reducing Seller's direct obligations under the SPA or changing the cap, basket, or escrow.
**Negotiation / implementation note:** Buyer should confirm the final policy form includes the waiver and that the fraud exception is limited to actual Seller fraud, consistent with the term sheet.
## Section 6.09 --- Non-Competition; Non-Solicitation
## 17. Section 6.09(a) --- Non-competition covenant scope (MEDIUM)
**Sources:** Executed Term Sheet §11; Playbook §10.1; partner instructions ¶¶237--246
**Seller's draft language:**

> \(a\) For a period of five (5) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, engage in, own, manage, operate, control, participate in, consult with, render services for, or in any manner be connected with any business anywhere in the United States; provided that ... passive public-company investment and performance under the Transaction Documents are permitted.
**Proposed buyer redline / replacement language:**
> Replace Section 6.09(a) with:

> \(a\) Non-Competition. For a period of three (3) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its controlled Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, engage in, own, manage, operate, finance, control, or participate in the ownership, management, operation, financing, or control of any business engaged in the provision of environmental remediation services or hazardous waste management services, in each case in the States of Oregon, Washington, California, or Nevada; provided that this Section 6.09(a) shall not restrict Seller or its Affiliates from (i) conducting their construction, timber, and other businesses as conducted as of the Closing Date, (ii) holding, solely as a passive investment, less than five percent (5%) of the outstanding equity securities of any publicly traded entity, or (iii) performing environmental-related activities that are incidental to and performed solely in connection with Seller's construction or timber operations, including erosion control, stormwater management, and environmental compliance activities at Seller's own sites. For the avoidance of doubt, this Section 6.09(a) shall not apply to any portfolio company or operating subsidiary of Seller that is not engaged in environmental remediation services or hazardous waste management services as of the Closing Date.

**Track-changes comment / rationale:** The draft's five-year nationwide restriction covering "any business" would sweep in Evergreen's unrelated construction and timber operations and raises enforceability concerns, particularly across Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada. The term sheet fixes a three-year period, four-state geography, and the specific business scope of environmental remediation and hazardous waste management services. The revised language tracks those negotiated limits and preserves the agreed carve-outs.

**Negotiation / implementation note:** The existing non-solicitation language is broader than the term sheet as to duration and customer/supplier restrictions. Partner instructions specifically require narrowing the non-compete; confirm whether the client also wants the non-solicit reduced from three years to the term sheet's two years and limited to Company employees.
# Additional Issues Requiring Discussion or Factual Cleanup
These items are not all part of the partner's numbered priority list, but they should be addressed before the buyer sends a definitive redline or finalizes disclosure schedules.
## A. Dalton Creek disclosure discrepancy --- immediate factual correction

**Seller's draft issue:** Schedule 4.15(d), Item 2 states that the Dalton Creek site is in Lane County and that the EPA information request is dated June 12, 2025. The diligence memo and executed term sheet identify the site as located in Clackamas County, Oregon and the request as dated February 12, 2025. The term sheet also describes the Dalton Creek Facility as the former operations site covered by the Special Indemnity.
**Proposed schedule replacement:**
> 2\. Dalton Creek Disposal Facility --- Clackamas County, Oregon.

> The Company received an information request from the United States Environmental Protection Agency, Region 10, dated February 12, 2025, pursuant to Section 104(e) of CERCLA, 42 U.S.C. § 9604(e), regarding the Company's former operations at the Dalton Creek disposal facility located in Clackamas County, Oregon (the "Dalton Creek Facility"). The information request seeks information regarding the types, quantities, characterization, handling, transportation, and disposal of hazardous wastes associated with the Company's former operations at the Dalton Creek Facility. As of the date hereof, no formal enforcement action, notice of potential responsibility, unilateral administrative order, consent decree, or lawsuit has been issued or filed against the Company in connection with the Dalton Creek Facility. The Company has engaged outside environmental counsel to assist in responding to the information request. Outside environmental counsel estimates the Company's potential liability, if designated as a potentially responsible party, at between \$1,500,000 and \$6,000,000, depending on the scope of remediation and allocation of responsibility among potentially responsible parties.

**Comment:** The discrepancy is material because the site location and date identify the environmental matter covered by the Special Indemnity. Confirm the correct facts with the Environmental Practice Group before circulating the markup. The Special Indemnity and all cross-references should use one consistent defined term and factual description.
## B. Hargrove project timeline discrepancy

**Issue:** The diligence memo describes approximately 18--24 months of remaining work after the anticipated Closing, while Schedule 4.15(d) states 24--36 months. Confirm the project schedule, remaining cost estimate (\$4.2 million), DEQ contract/task order, and insurance status. This affects the environmental survival and interim covenant analysis.
## C. Confidentiality Agreement date and Buyer address mismatch

- Term Sheet §17 refers to a Confidentiality Agreement dated July 12, 2025; SPA §6.03 refers to a Mutual Confidentiality Agreement dated June 20, 2025. Confirm which agreement governs and conform the recital/reference before execution.
- The term sheet lists Buyer's address as 200 South Wacker Drive, Suite 3100, Chicago, Illinois 60606; SPA §10.01 lists 210 South Wacker Drive. Confirm the correct notice address.
## D. Fund / financing description should be reconciled

The diligence memo identifies the transaction as a Whitmore Capital Partners LLC Fund III platform acquisition, while SPA §5.04 references an equity commitment from Whitmore Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. The term sheet identifies a \$125 million Clearwater Environmental Lending Corp. financing commitment but does not identify Fund IV. Confirm the correct financing and equity-commitment parties and update the SPA's Buyer representations, closing deliverables, and any lender collateral references. This is a factual and execution issue rather than a requested economic markup.
## E. Environmental permit schedule requires action tracking

Schedule 4.15(b) includes several permits with expirations near the anticipated Closing or shortly thereafter, including the Oregon UST permit, Oregon remediation contractor license, Washington Ecology contractor license, and California CUPA permit. Prepare a permit action tracker identifying the issuing agency, change-of-control notice deadline, approval requirement, renewal date, responsible party, filing status, and evidence of submission. The SPA covenant should be cross-checked against that tracker.
## F. PE-licensed personnel and key-person continuity

The draft represents that 12 PE licenses are in good standing but does not provide a retention or transition covenant for the personnel whose licenses are required for permit compliance. This is an additional diligence recommendation, not a current partner priority. Consider requiring Seller to disclose any notice of resignation or threatened departure by the 12 listed license holders and adding a covenant to use commercially reasonable efforts to retain them through Closing. Buyer should assess whether separate employment or retention agreements are needed for critical PE-licensed personnel.
# Negotiation Roadmap and Open Decisions

1.  Lead with the term-sheet deviations: 12.5% cap, Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, payoff letters, non-compete, and earnout operating covenant. These are the clearest commercial positions and should not be diluted in the first markup.
2.  Treat the MAE qualifiers and pro-sandbagging language as non-negotiable buyer protections. The environmental-sector playbook expressly requires both positions.

3.  Use the balanced government-contract position in the first draft: submissions and notifications before Closing, no adverse agency indication, and a post-Closing cooperation tail. Escalate to a hard novation condition if the client is willing to accept timing risk.

4.  Use 36 months as the environmental representation survival ask and reserve the full-applicable-statute position as a client/partner escalation. Maintain the 72-month Dalton Creek Special Indemnity independent of the general environmental survival period.

5.  Confirm the Dalton Creek and Hargrove factual discrepancies and the closing checklist items before finalizing schedules. The Dalton Creek discrepancy must be corrected in the SPA and the Special Indemnity schedule.
# Source Cross-Reference
The markup positions above are supported by the following source provisions:

- Executed Term Sheet dated September 10, 2025: §§4--6 (escrow and payoff), §5 (earnout), §§7--10 (representations, indemnification, Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, R&W insurance), §§11--13 (restrictive covenants, conditions, and covenants).

- Environmental DD Summary dated October 18, 2025: §§III (Dalton Creek), IV (Hargrove), V (23 environmental permits), VI (four government contracts and FAR novation), VII (insurance), and VIII (action items).
- Partner markup instructions dated October 23, 2025: priority issues 1--12 and "do not mark up" items.

'“Indemnification Cap” means Forty-Three Million Dollars ($43,000,000), which is equal to twenty percent (20%) of the Base Enterprise Value.',
'“Indemnification Cap” means Twenty-Six Million Eight Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars ($26,875,000), which is equal to twelve and one-half percent (12.5%) of the Base Enterprise Value.',

'The seller’s 20% / $43 million cap directly contradicts the executed term sheet, which fixes the general cap at 12.5% of the $215 million Base Enterprise Value, or $26.875 million. The playbook instructs that the executed term sheet controls economic terms and that a deviation must be corrected without treating it as a drafting gray area.',

'The cap is for Losses arising from breaches of non-Fundamental Representations. Fundamental Representation liability remains subject to the Purchase Price cap, and the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity must remain outside the general cap.'

add_issue(3, 'Section 2.05', 'Earnout covenant and financial mechanics', 'CRITICAL',
'Executed Term Sheet §5; Playbook §§7.1–7.2; partner instructions ¶¶88–111',
'''(c) Within sixty (60) days after the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall prepare and deliver to Seller a written statement … setting forth Buyer’s good-faith calculation of Adjusted EBITDA …

(d) From and after the Closing Date through the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall, and shall cause the Company to, operate the business of the Company in a manner consistent with past practice and in good faith to maximize the Earnout Payment. … Buyer shall cause the Company to maintain substantially the same level of personnel, equipment, and other resources … and shall not divert or redirect any contracts, customers, revenues, or business opportunities …
(e) Any Earnout Payment … shall be paid … within ten (10) Business Days after the final determination of Adjusted EBITDA …''',
'''Replace Section 2.05(c), (d), and (e) in their entirety with the following:

(c) Within forty-five (45) days following the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall prepare and deliver to Seller a written statement (the “Earnout Statement”) setting forth Buyer’s good-faith calculation of Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period and the resulting Earnout Payment, if any, together with reasonable supporting detail. Seller shall have thirty (30) days following receipt of the Earnout Statement to review the Earnout Statement and deliver a written notice of objection specifying in reasonable detail each disputed item and the amount Seller believes to be correct. Any dispute not resolved by the Parties within twenty (20) Business Days after delivery of such notice shall be submitted to the Independent Accountant under Section 2.04(c), whose determination shall be final and binding absent manifest error.

(d) Following the Closing, Buyer shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, take any action with the primary purpose of avoiding or reducing the Earnout Payment. For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this Section 2.05(d) shall restrict Buyer’s right to operate, integrate, restructure, or otherwise manage the Company and its business in Buyer’s sole discretion, including the right to make capital expenditure decisions, change pricing or compensation, make strategic investments, acquire or dispose of businesses or assets, reorganize the Company or its operations, allocate resources, or take any other operational action, and no such action shall constitute a breach of this Section 2.05(d) unless taken with the primary purpose of avoiding or reducing the Earnout Payment. Buyer shall have no affirmative obligation to operate the Company in any particular manner, to maximize the Earnout Payment, to maintain the Company as a separate entity, to maintain any particular level of personnel, equipment, capital expenditures, or resources, to retain any employee, or to refrain from diverting or redirecting contracts, customers, revenues, or business opportunities, in each case except to the extent an action is taken with the primary purpose of avoiding or reducing the Earnout Payment.

(e) Any Earnout Payment determined to be payable pursuant to this Section 2.05 shall be paid by Buyer to Seller within sixty (60) days following the end of the Earnout Period, subject to final determination under this Section 2.05, by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Seller. For U.S. federal income tax purposes, the Parties agree to treat any Earnout Payment as an adjustment to the Purchase Price.''',

'The seller’s affirmative operating obligations would effectively give Seller veto rights over Buyer’s platform integration, restructuring, personnel, capital allocation, and bolt-on strategy through December 31, 2026. The playbook permits only a narrow negative covenant against actions taken with the primary purpose of avoiding or reducing the earnout. The economic thresholds in the draft are correct ($25 million maximum; $38 million full-payment threshold; $32 million floor; linear interpolation), but the timing is not: the term sheet requires the calculation within 45 days and payment within 60 days after the Measurement Period. The replacement language preserves the agreed economics and restores Buyer’s operational flexibility.',

'Confirm that the final Exhibit D includes the agreed Adjusted EBITDA methodology and add-backs for buyer-directed integration costs, restructuring charges, non-recurring items, and post-closing affiliate/corporate allocations not charged consistently before Closing.'

'No specific covenant addresses the four Government Contracts, FAR 42.1204 novation requests, state change-of-control notices, or post-Closing cooperation. Section 6.05 only requires general third-party consent efforts.',
'''Add the following as new Section 6.05A:
Section 6.05A Government Contract Notifications, Novations, and Recognition.

(a) Promptly following the date of this Agreement, and in any event sufficiently in advance of the Closing to permit agency review, Seller shall cause the Company to notify each applicable contracting officer and Governmental Authority of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement and to submit all novation, recognition, change-of-control, change-of-name, or other requests, notices, applications, and supporting materials required under any Government Contract, applicable procurement Law, the Anti-Assignment Act, 41 U.S.C. § 6305, FAR Part 42, Subpart 42.12, or analogous state requirements. (d) Following the Closing, Seller shall continue to provide reasonable cooperation, information, records, personnel access, and executed documents reasonably requested by Buyer or the Company in connection with any pending novation, recognition, change-of-control notification, or related agency process, including participation in meetings with contracting officers, until all such processes have been completed or the applicable Governmental Authority has confirmed that no further action is required.''',

A hard condition requiring completed novations is reserved for discussion because FAR processing may take 60–120 days or longer and could conflict with the mid-January target and February 28 Outside Date.',

)

lines.text: # ---------- Article X and Section VI noncompete ----------
add_heading('Article X — Miscellaneous', level=2)
add_issue(16, 'New Section 10.13', 'R&W insurance subrogation waiver', 'MEDIUM',
'Executed Term Sheet §10; Playbook §§8.1–8.2; partner instructions ¶¶223–235',

'The draft contains no provision addressing Buyer’s representations and warranties insurance policy, Granite Ridge Underwriters, or waiver of insurer subrogation rights against Seller and its affiliates.',
'''Add the following as new Section 10.13:

Section 10.13 R&W Insurance; Subrogation Waiver. Buyer shall use commercially reasonable efforts to bind a representations and warranties insurance policy on or prior to the Closing Date in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement (the “R&W Insurance Policy”). If Buyer or any of its Affiliates obtains an R&W Insurance Policy, Buyer shall cause the R&W Insurance Policy to provide that the insurer thereunder irrevocably waives, and shall not exercise or pursue, any right of subrogation or other right of recovery against Seller or any of Seller’s Affiliates, directors, officers, employees, agents, or Representatives with respect to any claim made by Buyer or any Buyer Indemnitee under the R&W Insurance Policy, except to the extent such claim arises from or relates to actual Fraud by Seller. Buyer shall not amend, modify, terminate, or waive the R&W Insurance Policy in a manner that would adversely affect Seller’s rights under this Section 10.13 without Seller’s prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. The obligations of Buyer under this Section 10.13 shall survive the Closing for the term of the R&W Insurance Policy.''',

'The term sheet acknowledges Buyer’s R&W insurance placement and requires a subrogation waiver in favor of Seller and its related parties, except for Seller fraud. The draft is silent. The provision is standard market risk allocation and should be included without reducing Seller’s direct obligations under the SPA or changing the cap, basket, or escrow.',
'Buyer should confirm the final policy form includes the waiver and that the fraud exception is limited to actual Seller fraud, consistent with the term sheet.'
add_heading('Section 6.09 — Non-Competition; Non-Solicitation', level=2)
add_issue(17, 'Section 6.09(a)', 'Non-competition covenant scope', 'MEDIUM',
'Executed Term Sheet §11; Playbook §10.1; partner instructions ¶¶237–246',

'''(a) For a period of five (5) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, engage in, own, manage, operate, control, participate in, consult with, render services for, or in any manner be connected with any business anywhere in the United States; provided that … passive public-company investment and performance under the Transaction Documents are permitted.''',
'''Replace Section 6.09(a) with:

(a) Non-Competition. For a period of three (3) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its controlled Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, engage in, own, manage, operate, finance, control, or participate in the ownership, management, operation, financing, or control of any business engaged in the provision of environmental remediation services or hazardous waste management services, in each case in the States of Oregon, Washington, California, or Nevada; provided that this Section 6.09(a) shall not restrict Seller or its Affiliates from (i) conducting their construction, timber, and other businesses as conducted as of the Closing Date, (ii) holding, solely as a passive investment, less than five percent (5%) of the outstanding equity securities of any publicly traded entity, or (iii) performing environmental-related activities that are incidental to and performed solely in connection with Seller’s construction or timber operations, including erosion control, stormwater management, and environmental compliance activities at Seller’s own sites. For the avoidance of doubt, this Section 6.09(a) shall not apply to any portfolio company or operating subsidiary of Seller that is not engaged in environmental remediation services or hazardous waste management services as of the Closing Date.''',

'The draft’s five-year nationwide restriction covering “any business” would sweep in Evergreen’s unrelated construction and timber operations and raises enforceability concerns, particularly across Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada. The term sheet fixes a three-year period, four-state geography, and the specific business scope of environmental remediation and hazardous waste management services. The revised language tracks those negotiated limits and preserves the agreed carve-outs.',

'The existing non-solicitation language is broader than the term sheet as to duration and customer/supplier restrictions. Partner instructions specifically require narrowing the non-compete; confirm whether the client also wants the non-solicit reduced from three years to the term sheet’s two years and limited to Company employees.'
# ---------- additional issues ----------
add_heading('Additional Issues Requiring Discussion or Factual Cleanup', level=1)
add_p('These items are not all part of the partner’s numbered priority list, but they should be addressed before the buyer sends a definitive redline or finalizes disclosure schedules.')
add_heading('A. Dalton Creek disclosure discrepancy — immediate factual correction', level=2)

add_label_para('Seller’s draft issue: ', 'Schedule 4.15(d), Item 2 states that the Dalton Creek site is in Lane County and that the EPA information request is dated June 12, 2025. The diligence memo and executed term sheet identify the site as located in Clackamas County, Oregon and the request as dated February 12, 2025. The term sheet also describes the Dalton Creek Facility as the former operations site covered by the Special Indemnity.', fill='FCE4D6')
add_label_para('Proposed schedule replacement: ', '', fill='E2F0D9')
add_code('''2. Dalton Creek Disposal Facility — Clackamas County, Oregon.

The Company received an information request from the United States Environmental Protection Agency, Region 10, dated February 12, 2025, pursuant to Section 104(e) of CERCLA, 42 U.S.C. § 9604(e), regarding the Company’s former operations at the Dalton Creek disposal facility located in Clackamas County, Oregon (the “Dalton Creek Facility”). The information request seeks information regarding the types, quantities, characterization, handling, transportation, and disposal of hazardous wastes associated with the Company’s former operations at the Dalton Creek Facility. As of the date hereof, no formal enforcement action, notice of potential responsibility, unilateral administrative order, consent decree, or lawsuit has been issued or filed against the Company in connection with the Dalton Creek Facility. The Company has engaged outside environmental counsel to assist in responding to the information request. Outside environmental counsel estimates the Company’s potential liability, if designated as a potentially responsible party, at between $1,500,000 and $6,000,000, depending on the scope of remediation and allocation of responsibility among potentially responsible parties.''', fill='F5FBF2')

add_label_para('Comment: ', 'The discrepancy is material because the site location and date identify the environmental matter covered by the Special Indemnity. Confirm the correct facts with the Environmental Practice Group before circulating the markup. The Special Indemnity and all cross-references should use one consistent defined term and factual description.', fill='EAF2F8')
add_heading('B. Hargrove project timeline discrepancy', level=2)

add_label_para('Issue: ', 'The diligence memo describes approximately 18–24 months of remaining work after the anticipated Closing, while Schedule 4.15(d) states 24–36 months. Confirm the project schedule, remaining cost estimate ($4.2 million), DEQ contract/task order, and insurance status. This affects the environmental survival and interim covenant analysis.', fill='FFF2CC')
add_heading('C. Confidentiality Agreement date and Buyer address mismatch', level=2)
add_bullets([

'Term Sheet §17 refers to a Confidentiality Agreement dated July 12, 2025; SPA §6.03 refers to a Mutual Confidentiality Agreement dated June 20, 2025. Confirm which agreement governs and conform the recital/reference before execution.',
'The term sheet lists Buyer’s address as 200 South Wacker Drive, Suite 3100, Chicago, Illinois 60606; SPA §10.01 lists 210 South Wacker Drive. Confirm the correct notice address.',
add_heading('D. Fund / financing description should be reconciled', level=2)

add_p('The diligence memo identifies the transaction as a Whitmore Capital Partners LLC Fund III platform acquisition, while SPA §5.04 references an equity commitment from Whitmore Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. The term sheet identifies a $125 million Clearwater Environmental Lending Corp. financing commitment but does not identify Fund IV. Confirm the correct financing and equity-commitment parties and update the SPA’s Buyer representations, closing deliverables, and any lender collateral references. This is a factual and execution issue rather than a requested economic markup.')
add_heading('E. Environmental permit schedule requires action tracking', level=2)

add_p('Schedule 4.15(b) includes several permits with expirations near the anticipated Closing or shortly thereafter, including the Oregon UST permit, Oregon remediation contractor license, Washington Ecology contractor license, and California CUPA permit. Prepare a permit action tracker identifying the issuing agency, change-of-control notice deadline, approval requirement, renewal date, responsible party, filing status, and evidence of submission. The SPA covenant should be cross-checked against that tracker.')
add_heading('F. PE-licensed personnel and key-person continuity', level=2)

add_p('The draft represents that 12 PE licenses are in good standing but does not provide a retention or transition covenant for the personnel whose licenses are required for permit compliance. This is an additional diligence recommendation, not a current partner priority. Consider requiring Seller to disclose any notice of resignation or threatened departure by the 12 listed license holders and adding a covenant to use commercially reasonable efforts to retain them through Closing. Buyer should assess whether separate employment or retention agreements are needed for critical PE-licensed personnel.')
# ---------- negotiation roadmap ----------

add_numbered([

'Lead with the term-sheet deviations: 12.5% cap, Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, payoff letters, non-compete, and earnout operating covenant. These are the clearest commercial positions and should not be diluted in the first markup.',
'Treat the MAE qualifiers and pro-sandbagging language as non-negotiable buyer protections. The environmental-sector playbook expressly requires both positions.',
